item.title: Makinde Presents ₦1.115tn 2027 Budget To Oyo Assembly
item.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has presented a proposed budget of ₦1.115 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration and approval. Tagged the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, the proposal is valued at ₦1,115,341,378,359.90. Presenting the budget on Tuesday at the Assembly complex in Agodi, Ibadan, Makinde said it was designed to consolidate the gains of his administration and lay a foundation for sustainable development beyond its tenure. He described it as the final budget proposal of his administration, saying it would sustain the state’s development momentum and ensure continuity after the transition to a new government. “As we prepare to hand over the baton to the next administration, we bring before you the 2027 Budget of Sustained Progress. It is designed to consolidate our gains, sustain public services and carry our state’s development forward through the transition period and beyond,” he said. The governor said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, community development and the strengthening of public institutions, with significant allocations for capital projects in health, education and road infrastructure. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Makinde said Oyo State’s Internally Generated Revenue increased by 288 per cent, from ₦26.59 billion in 2019 to ₦103.25 billion in 2025. He also noted that the state ranked third nationally in the 2025 Subnational Ease of Doing Business Assessment. The governor said targeted interventions and partnerships had helped return about 65,000 out-of-school children to classrooms, alongside investments in educational infrastructure, recruitment and service delivery. He, however, said the administration’s performance should be measured beyond revenue figures and rankings. “Figures alone cannot fully assess our administration. The real measure of success is the impact we have made on the lives of our people and the institutions we have built to serve them beyond May 29, 2027,” he said. Makinde also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to women’s inclusion in governance, pledging to sustain the 35 per cent affirmative action policy for women. On infrastructure and agriculture, he said the government had prioritised strategic road projects to connect economic corridors, improve market access and create opportunities for farmers, businesses and rural communities. He said the establishment of the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency had helped reposition agriculture as a viable business sector, while the Oyo State Agribusiness Transformation Centre had become a hub for agricultural investment. item.content:encoded: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has presented a proposed budget of ₦1.115 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration and approval. Tagged the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, the proposal is valued at ₦1,115,341,378,359.90. Presenting the budget on Tuesday at the Assembly complex in Agodi, Ibadan, Makinde said it was designed to consolidate the gains of his administration and lay a foundation for sustainable development beyond its tenure. He described it as the final budget proposal of his administration, saying it would sustain the state’s development momentum and ensure continuity after the transition to a new government. “As we prepare to hand over the baton to the next administration, we bring before you the 2027 Budget of Sustained Progress. It is designed to consolidate our gains, sustain public services and carry our state’s development forward through the transition period and beyond,” he said. The governor said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, community development and the strengthening of public institutions, with significant allocations for capital projects in health, education and road infrastructure. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Makinde said Oyo State’s Internally Generated Revenue increased by 288 per cent, from ₦26.59 billion in 2019 to ₦103.25 billion in 2025. He also noted that the state ranked third nationally in the 2025 Subnational Ease of Doing Business Assessment. The governor said targeted interventions and partnerships had helped return about 65,000 out-of-school children to classrooms, alongside investments in educational infrastructure, recruitment and service delivery. He, however, said the administration’s performance should be measured beyond revenue figures and rankings. “Figures alone cannot fully assess our administration. The real measure of success is the impact we have made on the lives of our people and the institutions we have built to serve them beyond May 29, 2027,” he said. Makinde also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to women’s inclusion in governance, pledging to sustain the 35 per cent affirmative action policy for women. On infrastructure and agriculture, he said the government had prioritised strategic road projects to connect economic corridors, improve market access and create opportunities for farmers, businesses and rural communities. He said the establishment of the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency had helped reposition agriculture as a viable business sector, while the Oyo State Agribusiness Transformation Centre had become a hub for agricultural investment. According to him, the centre hosts 16 agribusinesses with investments valued at more than ₦20 billion, while over 30,000 farmers have been captured in the state’s agricultural database to improve planning and interventions. He added that the Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project (RAAMP) was improving access to markets, agricultural productivity and rural economies. In the health sector, the governor highlighted the induction of 3,933 newly recruited primary healthcare workers to strengthen service delivery and support investments in healthcare infrastructure. He also said construction work on several ongoing projects would accelerate during the dry season following approvals by the Executive to accommodate increased project costs arising from inflation, exchange rate fluctuations and rising energy prices. Makinde urged the Speaker and lawmakers to continue working with the Executive in the interest of residents and give the budget proposal expeditious consideration. In his remarks, the Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Adebo Ogundoyin, commended the governor for what he described as remarkable achievements since the beginning of his administration. Ogundoyin said the presentation marked the final budget cycle of the Omituntun 2.0 administration and provided an opportunity to consolidate seven and a half years of development across key sectors. He listed investments in road construction and rehabilitation, school infrastructure, healthcare facilities, agriculture and workers’ welfare among the achievements of the administration. The Speaker assured the governor that the Assembly would subject the proposal to thorough legislative scrutiny and give it the attention it deserved in the interest of the people. The event was attended by a former governor of the state and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, among other dignitaries. item.title: Why Chiefs are reportedly trading two picks for Colts WR Josh Downs
item.description: Why Chiefs are reportedly trading two picks for Colts WR Josh Downs originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs came into NFL trade deadline day with one very simple goal: acquire a wide receiver to help the offense. While Keenan Allen was dealt to the San Francisco 49ers , there was a different wide receiver from the Indianapolis Colts that they've had their eye on. Finally, with under half an hour to go, they made their move. According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer , the Chiefs are making a move for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs. In exchange for a pair of picks, the Chiefs are getting a new WR for Patrick Mahomes. Why Chiefs are trading for Josh Downs from Colts "Trade! The Chiefs are acquiring WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round and fifth-round picks, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports," Pelissero reports. Downs is a rental wide receiver for the Chiefs who instantly provides another solid weapon in the passing game for this offense. He'll join Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy in Kansas City, with running back Kenneth Walker III and tight end Travis Kelce making up a strong offensive supporting cast for Mahomes. The Chiefs are making this trade thanks in large part to Tyquan Thornton's season-ending injury. Add in that Worthy is banged up and has been underwhelming, and a WR addition was a must-have for this team. MORE : Harrison Butker keeps missing field goals and Chiefs fans have had enough A fourth-rounder and a fifth-rounder are a lot to give up for Downs for half a season and a seventh-round pick, but considering their major WR need and the other available options, this is a reasonable move for the Chiefs. Kansas City desperately needed WR help, and Downs might be the best WR traded in the middle of the 2026 season. Marvin Harrison Jr. went for a second-round pick and hasn't been great for the Houston Texans . The Chiefs, meanwhile, take a chance on Downs, who was having a down season with the Colts and their struggling offense. This move shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone, as the Chiefs were strongly implied as the favorites, and now, they're reportedly adding him in a huge move at the trade deadline. item.title: Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade reunion is a go as Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza
item.description: David Brytus-Imagn Images Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade reunion is a go as Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings were desperate to make a trade for a quarterback before the deadline after Monday night’s tough loss to the Buffalo Bills at home. Later in the day on Tuesday, they did just that , reuniting with a familiar face in the process. “Blockbuster! The Raiders are trading four-time Pro Bowl QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings for their 2027 third-round pick,” reported NFL insider Tom Pelissero of The Ringer on X, formerly Twitter. The move reunites the Vikings with Cousins after he spent multiple seasons there with head coach Kevin O’Connell, finding considerable success in the process. Minnesota’s defense has been elite this year but its offense has stumbled, with neither Kyler Murray nor Carson Wentz finding consistent success under center, making it clear that the team had to make a change before the deadline. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Meanwhile, this move now officially hands the keys to number one overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas. Mendoza has yet to make a start at the NFL level, but that will now change after he spent half of his rookie season learning behind Cousins. Cousins got off to a hot start to the year in Las Vegas, and although he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, he is still a competent veteran quarterback who should provide an upgrade for the Vikings immediately at the position. In any case, the Vikings will next hit the field on Sunday vs the Green Bay Packers, while Mendoza looks slated to make his first NFL start the same day vs the Seattle Seahawks. Related: Insider reveals how Vikings’ locker room is feeling after Kirk Cousins trade Related: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones fires back at George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr. injury conspiracy theories

item.title: Broncos trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers stands on the field during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s lead league insider, the Denver Broncos have traded for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. The Broncos will be sending a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick to the Chargers for Henley. Trade: Chargers are sending LB Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, per sources. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 10, 2026 Henley is a 6-0, 225-pound linebacker who was a third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2023 NFL Draft. Throughout his career, Henley has appeared in 56 games and totaled 317 tackles, 5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 4 interceptions, and 15 pass deflections during his time with the Chargers. This season, Henley has appeared in 8 games and totaled 51 tackles, 0.5 sacks, 1 forced fumble, 1 interception (which happened this past Sunday), and 2 pass deflections. Henley turns 27 years old here in a few days and is in the final year of his rookie deal, but figures to have a role in the Broncos’ defense moving forward. In the short term, Henley will play behind veteran starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , according to reports, but he is a talented linebacker who can cover and blitz, so he should earn some playing time rather quickly. The Broncos are sending a 2027 4th-round pick to the Chargers, but are expected to get a 4th-round compensation pick due to John Franklin-Myers signing with the Titans in free agency this offseason. I really like this pick. Henley is a talented player who gives the Broncos something they really need. An athletic linebacker with sideline-to-sideline speed that can cover and cover well. He’s an excellent coverage linebacker and can cover tight ends and running backs in the pass game, which has been a multi-year issue for the Broncos. Justin Strnad has graded out as one of the better coverage linebackers in the NFL, while Alex Singleton has struggled in that area. Singleton has been solid in the run game, but if he were to come off the field on third downs for Henley, I think that would improve the Broncos’ third-down defense. However, we have to see how the Broncos handle this moving forward, but obviously they have a vision for him since they traded for him. With Henley in the final year of his deal, and the fact that the Broncos traded a 4th-round pick for him, he seems like a player the team views as part of their future. Time will tell there, but it seems like a move for a player they plan on having beyond this season.

item.title: Patriots trade deadline tracker: News and rumors ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline
item.description: Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first two months of the regular season. While the expectation is that they will get several players back from injured reserve at some point, they also could go for a more radical approach in hopes of improving their team and gearing up for a stretch run in 2026. Like they have done multiple times in 2026 already, they could look at the trade market. Will there be additions to a list that already includes the likes of A.J. Brown, Jaylen Reed, Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse? Or could they move on from some of their players, like they did in 2025 ? We will know soon: the NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET. Until then, please make sure to bookmark and regularly revisit our Patriots trade deadline tracker for all the latest developments. item.title: Shawn Horcoff Addresses the Dylan Larkin Trade Standoff
item.description: Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff met with reporters at the NHL general managers’ meetings in Toronto on Tuesday, and nothing he said moved either of the two situations hanging over his roster. Asked about the Dylan Larkin trade standoff and Simon Edvinsson’s unsigned contract, Horcoff said it was “status quo” with both players. Oct 26, 2026; Edmonton, Alberta, CAN; Edmonton Oilers defensemen Ryan Shea (6) looks to clear the puck in front of Detroit Red Wings forward Dylan Larkin (71) during the second period at Rogers Place. Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Horcoff declined to comment on Dylan Larkin’s trade list The one detail that would tell everyone how close this is to ending stayed off the table. Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com reported that “Horcoff declined to comment on whether Larkin has altered the list of teams to which he would agree to be traded.” Horcoff did describe what a resolution has to look like from Detroit’s side. “Ideally, we get something that works for both sides, right?” he said . “But it has to be something that helps this team.” Larkin still has only 10 teams on his list The Red Wings would like Larkin to open up his approved list, and so far it has not changed. TSN’s Pierre LeBrun reported that Detroit has exhausted its options with the current 10 teams and would like to go deeper in talks with six to eight clubs outside them, while Larkin’s camp believes the list is already long enough. As long as it stays at 10, the market Detroit can actually work is small. Per LeBrun, the 10 teams are the New Jersey Devils, the Colorado Avalanche, the Vegas Golden Knights, the Dallas Stars, the Minnesota Wild, the Washington Capitals, the Utah Mammoth, the Carolina Hurricanes, the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Florida Panthers. Larkin is suspended without pay for now, which means Horcoff and the Red Wings can take their time with a trade. The 30-year-old center has played in 10 games this season for the Red Wings. Larkin scored two goals and recorded four assists with a plus-3 rating, according to ESPN . Horcoff still wants to sign Simon Edvinsson The other half of the status quo carries a hard date. Edvinsson, 23, is an unsigned restricted free agent working out in Nashville, and Cotsonika reported that the defenseman must sign by Dec. 1 to be eligible to play this season. Horcoff has said he has no interest in trading Edvinsson, and on Tuesday he did not close the door on listening. “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls,” Horcoff said. He added that his job is to do what is in the best interest of the Red Wings, and that he will take those calls and hear what other teams have to say.

Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Horcoff declined to comment on Dylan Larkin’s trade list The one detail that would tell everyone how close this is to ending stayed off the table. Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com reported that “Horcoff declined to comment on whether Larkin has altered the list of teams to which he would agree to be traded.” Horcoff did describe what a resolution has to look like from Detroit’s side. “Ideally, we get something that works for both sides, right?” he said . “But it has to be something that helps this team.” Larkin still has only 10 teams on his list The Red Wings would like Larkin to open up his approved list, and so far it has not changed. TSN’s Pierre LeBrun reported that Detroit has exhausted its options with the current 10 teams and would like to go deeper in talks with six to eight clubs outside them, while Larkin’s camp believes the list is already long enough. As long as it stays at 10, the market Detroit can actually work is small. Per LeBrun, the 10 teams are the New Jersey Devils, the Colorado Avalanche, the Vegas Golden Knights, the Dallas Stars, the Minnesota Wild, the Washington Capitals, the Utah Mammoth, the Carolina Hurricanes, the Tampa Bay Lightning and the Florida Panthers. Larkin is suspended without pay for now, which means Horcoff and the Red Wings can take their time with a trade. The 30-year-old center has played in 10 games this season for the Red Wings. Larkin scored two goals and recorded four assists with a plus-3 rating, according to ESPN . Horcoff still wants to sign Simon Edvinsson The other half of the status quo carries a hard date. Edvinsson, 23, is an unsigned restricted free agent working out in Nashville, and Cotsonika reported that the defenseman must sign by Dec. 1 to be eligible to play this season. Horcoff has said he has no interest in trading Edvinsson, and on Tuesday he did not close the door on listening. “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls,” Horcoff said. He added that his job is to do what is in the best interest of the Red Wings, and that he will take those calls and hear what other teams have to say.

item.title: Kyle Busch’s Hauler Drives Away For The Final Time At Homestead
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The No. 8 hauler left Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday night for the very last time, marking a somber end to the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season. After the championship race concluded, the 1.5-mile track was exited by this massive truck, which bore the signature of the late Kyle Busch, as it drove through the tunnel. Fans watched a video by Motorsport showing the team loading up the equipment out of deep respect for the driver who won 234 races across the top three series before his sudden death in May. Austin Hill took over the ride for Richard Childress Racing, piloting the No. 33 Chevrolet to a 15th-place finish in the finale. The team changed the car number from 8 to 33 to honor Busch, yet they kept the old hauler on site until this final departure. In 2027, Hill is scheduled to return full-time to the No. 33, shouldering a season marked by both a championship and a tragedy. His best effort this year came at Talladega with a 14th-place result, but Sunday was about saying goodbye. A Season of Highs and Lows The 2026 season will forever be remembered for two Kyles: Kyle Larson’s dominant playoff surge and Kyle Busch’s shocking death. Larson clinched his third Cup Series title during the opening stage of the finale, finishing 12th at Homestead-Miami Speedway to cap a 49-point victory over Christopher Bell. Even though Larson became the 11th driver in history to win three titles, he refused to look back at his achievements while the sport mourned. “I just feel like when you’re in it and you’re competing, it’s just so hard to reflect in the moment,” Larson said, according to a report . He added that he still has more to accomplish and plans to keep looking out the windshield rather than stopping to admire the rearview mirror. The championship celebration at the annual awards banquet on Tuesday will likely name Busch the most popular driver, honoring a man who died after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis. Final Tributes At The Track NASCAR leadership made sure the memory of “Rowdy” stayed front and center during the final race. Every fan in the grandstands received a No. 8 Busch flag, and a memorial graphic dedicated to him was painted directly on the frontstretch. The NBC TV booth observed a silent Lap 8 in his honor, with many attendees holding up eight fingers to pay tribute to the two-time champion. “It’s tough to not talk about Kyle when you’re back in Miami,” NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell said. He described Busch as an extraordinary competitor who won the championship at this very track and left a forever mark on the sport. O’Donnell admitted that celebrating a championship feels different without him, noting that the community still misses him deeply. Busch won both of his Cup titles in 2015 and 2019 at Homestead, making his final farewell at this venue even more poignant.

item.title: Steelers WR trade target dealt to Chiefs
item.description: (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have been at the center of wide receiver trade rumors for several weeks, with one of the primary names being Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts. However, Downs will not be a Steeler, as he has been traded to the Kansas City Chiefs. Kansas City sent fourth and fifth-round picks to the Colts in exchange for Downs and a seventh. The Chiefs lost wide receiver Tyquan Thornton to an ankle injury earlier this season, and their remaining receivers have been dreadful. Of 145 receivers to run at least 50 routes, Andrew Armstrong ranks 141st in yards per route run , while Jalen Royals is 130th. With less than 20 minutes to the trade deadline, it doesn’t appear the Steelers will pull off a trade, unless one comes together in the final minutes. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! item.title: Chargers trade LB Daiyan Henley to Broncos for ‘27 4th, ‘28 5th
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts during the second half against the Houston against the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ryan Sun/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers ended up trading away one of their players after all. Per several NFL insiders, the Bolts are sending linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Henley was originally a third-round pick back in 2023 out of Washington State and has been the team’s starting middle linebacker since the 2024 season. BREAKING: The #Chargers are trading LB Daiyan Henley to the #Broncos for the 4th and 5th round pick, per sources. https://t.co/oYhQDHu4En pic.twitter.com/9gPHPaxo9b — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 10, 2026 Henley is also a team captain and the “green dot” player who calls the defense for the Chargers. At the same time, Henley is currently in the final deal of his rookie contract and no real attempts at an extension had ever come to the table. Through the team’s eight games this season, Henley has been their leading tackler with 51. He has also posted two tackles for loss, a half sack, two pass breakups, an interception, a forced fumble, and two fumble recoveries. He now joins former Chargers running back JK Dobbins in Denver.

item.title: Colts reportedly trading WR Josh Downs to Chiefs after receiver requested a trade
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts lines up against the Tennessee Titans. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Justin Casterline via Getty Images Josh Downs is the latest player to leave Indianapolis after the Colts reportedly dealt the wide receiver to the Kansas City Chiefs, according to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport . Per Tom Pelissero , the Chiefs, who are also acquiring a 2027 seventh-round draft pick, are sending a fourth- and fifth-round pick in 2027 back to Indianapolis. The addition of the two picks will give the Colts a total of 13 in the 2027 draft. They still do not have a first-round selection after trading it to the New York Jets last season in the Sauce Gardner deal. Downs posted on social media after reports of the trade broke and was very relieved the matter was finally over. pic.twitter.com/SWGjirDe9N — JD (@JoshDowns) November 10, 2026 The 25-year-old Downs, who is set to become a free agent in the offseason, requested a trade away. His move follows the exits of guard Quenton Nelson , defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wide receiver Keenan Allen , who have been shipped out with the team off to a 2-7 start. Downs was the Colts' third-round pick in the 2023 draft out of North Carolina. He recorded 1,574 receiving yards on 140 catches and seven touchdowns over his first two seasons. This season, with Alec Pierce out due to injury, Downs led the Colts with 354 receiving yards and 57 targets. This story will be updated

item.title: 😳 384 logos on one shirt? Club plans craziest stunt ever
item.description: 😳 384 logos on one shirt? Club plans craziest stunt ever Why have one big main sponsor when you can have 384 (!)? Yes, you read that right: Brazilian club São Joseense, from the state of Paraná, is flipping the script for the 2027 season. Instead of signing a single mega-deal, the club is turning its new shirt into a colorful mosaic for the local community, with a whopping 384 advertising spaces. Each advertising space measures a compact 3.5 by 3.5 centimeters. Depending on whether the logo takes pride of place on the chest or ends up nearer the hem, interested sponsors will pay between 2,000 and 15,000 reais (roughly €300 to €2,500). But what is the club hoping to achieve? According to a press release, the aim is to give small businesses the chance to buy advertising space on the club's shirt. "Being a main sponsor costs a lot of money, which severely limits who can get involved. Our shirt project now gives microbusiness owners and sports enthusiasts an affordable way in," explained Eduardo Grassi. The club's managing director also emphasized: "We want business owners and fans to feel part of this sporting journey—in a city that lives and breathes football but has until now lacked a team of its own to identify with. This is another step toward making São Joseense more prominent and better equipped for a year full of sporting challenges awaiting us in 2027." Among other things, the club will make its debut in the prestigious Brazilian cup competition, the Copa do Brasil. For the mini-sponsors, that means exposure and TV airtime that microbusinesses can usually only dream of. Once the design is finalized, the shirts may well look like a giant QR code from a distance. But in the stands and among local businesses, the initiative is probably already creating exactly what every club hopes for: the feeling of being out on the pitch together. 📸 Instagram São Joseense This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: 'Lazy' Man City charges claim rebuffed as Premier League punishment wait continues amid appeal
item.description: Manchester City await any potential punishment(s) after an independent panel found the club guilty of allegedly breaching the Premier League's financial rules -Credit:NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images A sport integrity expert has emphasized that delays in publishing Manchester City's punishment for violating the Premier League's financial regulations are not because decision-makers are 'lazy'. Back in September, it was confirmed that City had been found guilty of nearly all of the Premier League charges brought against them. The independent panel determined City had intended to breach financial rules by inflating revenues or reducing costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion at the current exchange rate), through a series of 'sham' arrangements. City have appealed the decision and have maintained their innocence. As the appeal process unfolds, City fans have anxiously been awaiting their club's punishment. Given the volume of charges and the unprecedented nature of the case, several 'likely' sanctions have been discussed including; substantial points deductions, transfer bans, expulsion from the Premier League, and fines. Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino has buyout clause as Manc United debate Michael Carrick's future -Credit:Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images But speaking to the Press Association, co-founder and global chief executive of Sport Integrity Global Alliance (SIGA), Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros stressed the priority must be for justice to be served, rather than for a swift outcome to be achieved, as per the Manchester Evening News . "I understand the fans' frustration, and I understand also the fans' anguish, especially those who follow and support Manchester City," he said. "This is not a pleasant situation for anybody, but the law is the law, and it must be served on its own time, without constraints. Being a lawyer, I know that justice sometimes is served slowly. That is not because those who are in charge of the procedures are lazy, or they neglect their duties. It's because there cannot be room for doubt. There cannot be room for failure. "There cannot be any breach of the constitutional rights that those who are being scrutinised or judged enjoy. But I think it's fair to say that the process is coming to an end." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE The verdict determined that City operated a 'disguised funding scheme' whereby Abu Dhabi-based companies contributed only a portion of the figures recorded in the club's accounts, with the remaining balance covered by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), the vehicle through which Sheikh Mansour holds ownership of the club. This arrangement was found to have artificially inflated revenues by more than £830 million ($1.1 billion) across the nine-season stretch between 2009-10 and 2017-18. Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac address Wrexham executive’s abrupt exit USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino has buyout clause as Manc United debate Michael Carrick's future -Credit:Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images But speaking to the Press Association, co-founder and global chief executive of Sport Integrity Global Alliance (SIGA), Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros stressed the priority must be for justice to be served, rather than for a swift outcome to be achieved, as per the Manchester Evening News . "I understand the fans' frustration, and I understand also the fans' anguish, especially those who follow and support Manchester City," he said. "This is not a pleasant situation for anybody, but the law is the law, and it must be served on its own time, without constraints. Being a lawyer, I know that justice sometimes is served slowly. That is not because those who are in charge of the procedures are lazy, or they neglect their duties. It's because there cannot be room for doubt. There cannot be room for failure. "There cannot be any breach of the constitutional rights that those who are being scrutinised or judged enjoy. But I think it's fair to say that the process is coming to an end." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE The verdict determined that City operated a 'disguised funding scheme' whereby Abu Dhabi-based companies contributed only a portion of the figures recorded in the club's accounts, with the remaining balance covered by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), the vehicle through which Sheikh Mansour holds ownership of the club. This arrangement was found to have artificially inflated revenues by more than £830 million ($1.1 billion) across the nine-season stretch between 2009-10 and 2017-18. City were additionally found to have overstated image rights income by almost £74 million ($98.8 million), and understated staff contract liabilities by almost £17 million ($22.7 million). In response, the Blues maintained the ruling contained 'clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe'. Club CEO Ferran Soriano addressed staff via video, asserting that the panel had sided with the Premier League's 'conspiracy theory'.

item.title: Seattle Seahawks 2026 trade deadline tracker
item.description: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. For the second year in a row, the trade deadline is during Week 10. The Seattle Seahawks are usually active during the deadline, and this year they’ve pulled off one major trade. Will John Schneider cook up another midseason masterclass like he did for Leonard Williams, Quandre Diggs, Carlos Dunlap, and other names from previous deadline deals? Follow Field Gulls’ trade tracker coverage throughout Monday and Tuesday, and we’ll see what the Seahawks will do as they look to get back on track after a sputtering 5-4 start. Have the Seattle Seahawks made any trades during the regular season? Yes. They acquired longtime Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Who could the Seahawks potentially put on the trade block? No one immediately springs to mind. The likes of Dante Fowler Jr have rarely played this year but likely wouldn’t fetch much on the trade market. Emanuel Wilson being an unofficial healthy scratch is worth monitoring, although similarly he’s not much of a valuable trade piece, and Seattle may not want to risk moving any capable RB given the injury concerns on the depth chart. Which positions would the Seahawks potentially be most interested in? Edge rusher and wide receiver might be two positions of need for Seattle. Rashid Shaheed’s injury and generally underwhelming receiving stats could impact what Seattle does at receiver. The edge rushing room is essentially three deep, and with only Derick Hall and Connor O’Toole under contract beyond 2027, there might be some forward thinking required. The New York Jets’ Will McDonald IV has reportedly requested a trade and could be one to watch. When does the NFL trade deadline window close? At 4 pm ET/1 pm PT on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Latest Seattle Seahawks trade news Notable NFL trade news (Nov. 10) Josh Downs is going from the Indianapolis Colts to the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs will give up a fourth- and fifth-rounder and also get a seventh-rounder in return. The Denver Broncos land Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for a 2027 fourth- and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Kirk Cousins is going to the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 third-rounder , which means the Seahawks will not face Cousins this Sunday. Fernando Mendoza figures to make his first NFL start. item.title: Can Vikings still make the playoffs? What trade for Kirk Cousins means for Minnesota’s outlook
item.description: Can Vikings still make the playoffs? What trade for Kirk Cousins means for Minnesota’s outlook originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One day after seeing their offense stumble against one of football's most porous defensive units en route to defeat against the Bills , the Vikings are making major changes to their quarterback room. Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders , dealing a third-round pick in the other direction to land its former standout. The move constitutes a minor risk for the Vikings, who have struggled to get their collection of gifted pass-catchers — namely Justin Jefferson — involved in the attack in recent weeks. Minnesota's offensive foibles resurfaced during its 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. While the Vikings' defense performed admirably, their attack was notably more toothless, failing to mount much of a challenge against Buffalo's much-maligned backline. While Cousins has his detractors, he should prove more capable of throwing the ball downfield than the likes of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. His familiarity with head coach Kevin O'Connell's playbook should help him surge to the top of Minnesota's QB depth chart upon arrival — a place he's more than familiar with. With that, here's a look at how the Vikings can capitalize on Cousins' acquisition to surge to the playoffs. MORE: NFL trade deadline grades Can Vikings still make playoffs? Date Opponent Time Sun., Nov. 15 at Packers 1 p.m. Sun., Nov. 22 vs. 49ers 8:20 p.m. Sun., Nov. 29 vs. Falcons 1 p.m. Sun., Dec. 6 vs. Panthers 4:25 p.m. Thurs., Dec. 10 at Patriots 8:15 p.m. Sun., Dec. 20 vs. Lions 8:20 p.m. TBD vs. Commanders TBD Sun., Jan. 3 at Jets 1 p.m. TBD vs. Bears TBD Minnesota's 6-2 record belies Super Bowl contention. Its offensive exploits through nine games suggest otherwise. The Vikings are locked into a playoff spot thus far, sitting pretty at 6-2. They'll have ample adversaries vying for their spot, namely the Seahawks and the Rams . The Vikings' postseason hopes don't entirely rest upon Cousins' broad shoulders. The Brian Flores-led defense remains elite, holding the high-octane Bills attack to a season-low in points despite failing to receive any real production from the offense. Barring poor health, Minnesota should receive enough from its backline to stay in games. Cousins, instead, will be tasked with providing the fairy dust the Vikings' attack has desperately needed. He enjoyed a sizzling stint in Sin City, putting him on pace to tally a career-high in passing touchdowns. If he can at all rekindle that form in Minnesota — or close to it — the Vikings should be able to see out enough contests to keep their place among the NFC's elite (or scale even higher heights). Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . JUMP TO: Completed trades before NFL deadline Latest NFL trade deadline rumors NFL trade deadline deals by team Best players available at 2026 NFL trade deadline When is the NFL trade deadline in 2026? The NFL trade deadline is quickly approaching, giving teams one last chance to make deals for the postseason stretch. In recent years, the NFL trade deadline has increased in excitement as more teams have become willing to make moves during the season. That has continued this year, as there have already been major moves as contenders aim to strengthen their rosters for the second half and the playoffs. Thus far, the biggest trade story has been the Indianapolis Colts , who have sold a few pieces amid a disappointing season. They still have one of the biggest names available, though, as Jonathan Taylor could be traded if Indianapolis finds a team to pay its asking price. Taylor is not the only running back in rumors, though, with Derrick Henry also facing a trade possibility if the Baltimore Ravens want to sell the impending free agent. So far, the Ravens have been unwilling to trade the star as they hope to still compete down the stretch. The trade deadline will come and pass on Tuesday afternoon, and now that Week 9 is wrapping up, teams can focus on making deals in the final few days before the deadline. The Sporting News is tracking live updates on the latest NFL trade rumors ahead of the 2026 deadline. Follow along below with the news. NFL trade rumors before 2026 deadline Chiefs secure WR Josh Downs Date : Nov. 10 Source : Tom Pelissero The Chiefs are sending the Colts a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick for Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick. Kansas City is much improved this year but badly needed help in the wide receiver room, so they get the talented pending free agent in Downs. Broncos get Daiyan Henry from Chargers Date : Nov. 10 Source : Adam Schefter Denver gets linebacker help in the form of Henry, sending a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick back to the Chargers in return. Los Angeles was hesitant to sell but agreed to this deal before the deadline. Colts will not trade Jonathan Taylor Date : Nov. 10 Source : Tom Pelissero The Colts received offers headlined by second-round picks, but the team opted to keep their star for the remainder of the season. Indianapolis has just two wins and is clearly in rebuild mode, making Taylor one of the few reasons to watch the team. Kirk Cousins heads back to the Vikings Date : Nov. 10 Source : Tom Pelissero The Vikings get Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick, bringing the former Minnesota QB back to try and help fix the offense. Cousins spent 2018-2023 with the team, leading Minnesota to multiple playoff appearances. Bills snag safety Amani Hooker Date : Nov. 10 Source : Tom Pelissero The full deal sees the Titans sending Hooker and a fifth-round pick to the Bills for a second-round pick. Hooker has been one of the best Titans all season, as he even intercepted Joe Burrow three times in the same game earlier in the year. 49ers land Keenan Allen from Colts Date : Nov. 10 Source : Tom Pelissero San Francisco sends Indianapolis a sixth-round pick for Allen, who will be playing for his fourth team with the 49ers. Allen is a veteran who gives the 49ers some experience down the stretch. Vikings have yet to make call to Saints about Derek Carr Date: Nov. 10 Source: Mike Florio Minnesota's quarterbacking woes have brought about a host of wacky rumors, one of which links the franchise with retired hurler Derek Carr. Florio reported that Minnesota hasn't placed a call for the aging passer. He remains on New Orleans' reserved/retired list, meaning the Vikings would have to trade for him to land his services. Tyreek Hill lurking in the shadows, per agent Date: Nov. 10 Source: Drew Rosenhaus Hill has yet to be medically cleared from the dislocated knee he suffered last year, but is anticipating receiving the thumbs up to return in a few weeks, according to his agent, Drew Rosenhaus. That could open the door to him returning to the field as a free agent. Cowboys considering signing Kendre Miller as RB2 Date: Nov. 10 Source: Todd Archer The Cowboys are in the market for a new tailback after backup Tyler Goodson suffered a knee injury in Week 9. Per Archer, Dallas is looking at Miller, who was recently a casualty of waivers. The former Saints running back tallied 159 yards and two touchdowns on 57 carries this season before getting purged. Chargers may be willing to listen to offers Date : Nov. 10 Source : Jordan Schultz Schultz reports that Los Angeles seems more "receptive" to offers in the last 24 hours and could trade players if the deal is right. While the Chargers remain the lone team in the NFL without a win, they haven't appeared interested in moving players yet. Bengals back out of Ebiketie deal Date : Nov. 10 Source : Adam Schefter It turns out, Cincinnati didn't want Ebiketie to mean the team loses a third-round compensatory pick, so the team backed out of the deal. The comp pick formula could end up impacting the Bengals' plans today. Commanders 'unlikey' to make any significant moves Date : Nov. 10 Source : Ben Standig At 2-5-1, the Commanders' season is going in the wrong direction, but Washington does not appear inclined to make any of their players available. The Commanders have many veterans they could explore trading if they do change their mind. Be

item.title: Santi Aldama Fixes Dallas Offense After Brutal Losses
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Dallas Mavericks finally found their rhythm on Sunday night, crushing the Brooklyn Nets by a staggering 37-point margin. This 130-93 victory marks the team’s largest winning streak of the season so far. Following a slump marked by consecutive defeats against the Sacramento Kings and San Antonio Spurs, the victory arrives. Per The Smoking Cuban , this sharp turnaround coincides directly with the return of Santi Aldama to the starting lineup. Aldama is filling a roster spot and solving specific problems that plagued the offense all year. The team struggled mightily in their last game against Utah, shooting just 41.9 percent from the field and a poor 28.1 percent from three-point range. However, the energy shifted instantly when Aldama got back on the court. According to The Smoking Cuban , the Mavericks have improved considerably in offensive rebounding and second-chance points specifically because of his presence. The Second-Chance Fix For a long time, Dallas could not secure loose balls near the rim. Throughout the whole league last year, the squad placed 22nd for offensive rebounding and 24th for second-chance points. One year prior, the Mavericks ranked among the NBA’s poorest scoring teams after a missed shot. That stat line has flipped in a hurry. Against the Utah Jazz, Dallas outrebounded the opponent 21-8 on the offensive glass. This dominance led to a massive 21-5 advantage in second-chance points. Aldama alone grabbed nine rebounds in that game, with four of them coming on the offensive end. Versatility Creates Mismatches The big man’s size alone gives Dallas a bonus that other teams cannot match. He is not pigeonholed into playing only center or power forward, which changes how the offense flows. His shooting skill enables Aldama to occupy the three position, He played even when paired with Morez Johnson Jr. in lineups and Daniel Gafford. His perimeter game was on full display against Brooklyn, where he scored 12 points. He shot 5-of-7 from the floor and hit 2-of-4 from three-point range. Aldama scored in a variety of ways, including a basket off a dribble drive that showed his unique skill set. A New Offensive Identity The length and versatility Aldama brings have already stood out in these recent wins. The 7-foot big man helps the team handle defensive pressure and creates easy looks for teammates. His ability to stretch the floor opens up driving lanes for guards who were previously clogged. The improvement in both rebounding and scoring options suggests the team is only getting better. Per The Smoking Cuban, Aldama is a key reason the Mavericks are now two games above .500.

item.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
item.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. No. 15 Oregon (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) hosts No. 23 UCLA (4-0, 2-0) at 12:30 p.m. on Oct. 10. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselv
item.content:encoded: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that! The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind. Although, admittedly, Cronin’s biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market. The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later. Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can’t. Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent . And if he does, the Blazers can either trade him for pieces that fit better or clear out the logjam and build around him. But to sell the current roster as a basketball strategy doesn’t quite pass the smell test. Neither Lillard nor Morant has achieved stardom due to his defensive acumen. Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary. So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction. And if you’re being honest, you probably don’t need to wonder which of the two it is. “We were very focused and we’ll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can,” Cronin said. That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks. But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard’s career? “Dame literally just wants to win,” said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. “I think that’s the only thing left he really has to (do). He’s already proven he’s a winner, but at the highest level.” Does adding Morant move Lillard closer to a title? Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon? Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. If it becomes clear that Morant is one point guard too many, or that he’s just not the player he once was, some will argue that it didn’t cost the Blazers much to try. However, there is an opportunity cost to messing with Lillard’s swan song. If you don’t get it right, you risk wasting the gift of his voluntary return last summer . And, not for nothing, Lillard has the option to become a free agent again after this season. The franchise icon certainly hasn’t said anything that would suggest he is unhappy about Morant’s presence, although he stopped short on Monday of a full-throated endorsement. He said he knew about the trade before it went through. When I asked if he thought it was a good idea right away or if he needed time to get on board with the plan, Lillard said, “My position on it was, I’m prepared for whatever.” It’s good that he’s already thinking about other positions. Because his old one is getting awfully crowded. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . Add oregonlive.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn’t create success for our team this season.” Latest Ducks news Dan Lanning backs expanded college football playoff to 24 teams Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham takes shot at Oregon’s $50M roster Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: Parrott in running for hat-trick at FAI awards
item.description: Parrott is nominated for player of the year, young player of the year and goal of the year [Getty Images] Troy Parrott has been shortlisted in three categories for the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) International Awards. The 24-year-old Real Betis striker is in the running for player of the year and young player of the year, while he has two nominations for goal of the year. Parrott helped propel the Republic of Ireland into the World Cup playoffs, scoring both goals in the victory over Portugal in Dublin before netting a hat-trick in the must-win away game against Hungary, while also finding the net from the spot in the play-off defeat by Czech Republic. The Dubliner is a first-time nominee in the player of the year category, joined by Dara O'Shea who also makes the list for the first time, while goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher makes the shortlist for the second year. James Abankwah and Evan Ferguson - who won in 2022 and 2023 - join Parrott on the young player of the year shortlist. Parrott's second goal and last-gasp winner away to Hungary are in consideration for goal of the year along with Katie McCabe's stunning stike in the 3-2 away win against Poland in a World Cup qualifier. The women's national team captain is nominated for women's senior player of the year for a sixth time and the 2021 winner is joined by first-time nominees Emily Murphy and Marissa Sheva. Women's young player of the year will be contested between 2024 winner Jessie Stapleton, three-time nominee Abbie Larkin and Emily Murphy who is included for the first time. Jacob Devaney, Mason Melia and Jamie Mullins are nominated for the men's under-21 award. The performances taken into account for all categories are from June 2025 to May 2026

item.title: Mariners Are Most Obvious Team for Red Sox to Make Blockbuster Trade With
item.description: Mariners Are Most Obvious Team for Red Sox to Make Blockbuster Trade With originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Boston Red Sox expected to have some needs on the mound, and Sonny Gray expected to depart in free agency, the front office has a few ways to approach this winter. There are a couple of decent starting pitchers out there, but outside of Tarik Skubal, there isn't exactly a lights-out pitcher on this free agency market. There are a couple of intriguing names on the potential trade market, however, with the Seattle Mariners having two of them. It would be questionable for the Mariners to move on from George Kirby or Emerson Hancock, but Seattle has other needs in the offense and could be willing to trade some of those guys for the right package. Whether it would be Seattle getting prospects back or big league talent is one thing, but either way, the Red Sox could be of interest to both of those teams. “The Red Sox built their team on pitching and defense, and they shouldn't go away from that plan in 2027 just because they need to upgrade the offense. The Seattle Mariners have multiple starting pitchers with at least two years of team control that they are willing to listen on. Acquiring one to add to Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, and Ranger Suarez would be one of the best rotations in baseball. “The Mariners reportedly want to use one of their pitchers to find an impact bat for their lineup. Breslow could kill two birds with one stone by using one of the outfielders to give them just that. The Red Sox can't go into 2027 with the amount of uncertainty in the bottom two of the rotation they currently have, and getting one of the Mariners' starters would be an excellent long-term fix to that situation,” Brian Burrows wrote . As Burrows noted, the Mariners looking for an offensive player who can come in and help immediately would give the Red Sox multiple options to move on from. Even if they wanted to go the prospect route, there are a few prospects in the Red Sox system who can help out Seattle in the short and long term. For Boston, the bigger thing here would be getting one of these two guys who have elite stuff. Kirby is coming off a season in which he struggled, posting a 4.33 ERA. However, if he can get back to his 2023 and 2024 form, there's reason to believe he can be an elite arm in this Red Sox rotation, especially since he's still just 28. item.title: LIV Golf Shuts Down: The End Of A Five-Year Experiment
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images LIV Golf officially closed up shop on November 5, marking the end of a five-year experiment funded by Saudi Arabia. The league launched with big promises and huge checks, but it could not sustain itself without its primary financial backer. This sudden halt leaves players scrambling for their next moves while the PGA Tour watches from the sidelines. ESPN staff writer Paolo Uggetti shared the details on why the league shut down, noting that the financial support from the Public Investment Fund has dried up. Saudi Arabia’s global sports influence shift was contextualized by Sarath Ganji, who founded the Autocracy and Global Sports Initiative, during this era. The money that once flowed freely to sign top talent is no longer available, forcing an orderly winding-down process. A Failed Vision and a New Reality The dream of a new era for professional golf died quickly once the funding stopped. Phil Mickelson proclaimed LIV would be a game changer that brought the PGA Tour to its knees, but that never happened. It was never destined to become the “force for change and good,” that Bryson DeChambeau once mocked so laughably. According to Lee News Central , LIV amounted to nothing beyond a cash grab. Because it was always amoral at its core and utterly devoid of principles, failure was inevitable like so many other things. From the beginning, Rory McIlroy, who became golf’s conscience through his fierce opposition to LIV, anticipated the conclusion. “I think that there is going to be a bit of a reset here, just for things to be a little bit more sustainable,” McIlroy said on Wednesday, November 4, when it became clear LIV was circling the drain. Players Pivot to New Deals With the league gone, players are already looking for new ways to make money. While he had previously collaborated with the brand on headcovers, this new deal expands their relationship to feature his own dedicated clothing collection. DeChambeau shared seven photographs announcing the news on social media alongside an enthusiastic message for his followers. “I’m excited for this one,” he wrote. “Headcovers were just the start… now I’m expanding my partnership with @swaggolfco into apparel!” The new collection drops November 19 online and in stores at Dick’s Sporting Goods and Golf Galaxy. Despite the league ending, DeChambeau insisted he had no regrets about joining in the summer of 2022. “I’m not going to rewrite the last four years. I made a decision I believed in, and I’m grateful for what came with it,” he wrote. Some might argue the lack of a financial war is bad for players, but McIlroy disagrees. “There’s not as much of an arms race as there was maybe a couple of years ago, and some players will argue that that’s not good for players. I think that’s very short-term thinking,” McIlroy said. “If you want sustainable tours, and we want these tours around in 50 years’ time, there has to be sustainable business practices in place to make sure they are.”
item.content:encoded: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images LIV Golf officially closed up shop on November 5, marking the end of a five-year experiment funded by Saudi Arabia. The league launched with big promises and huge checks, but it could not sustain itself without its primary financial backer. This sudden halt leaves players scrambling for their next moves while the PGA Tour watches from the sidelines. ESPN staff writer Paolo Uggetti shared the details on why the league shut down, noting that the financial support from the Public Investment Fund has dried up. Saudi Arabia’s global sports influence shift was contextualized by Sarath Ganji, who founded the Autocracy and Global Sports Initiative, during this era. The money that once flowed freely to sign top talent is no longer available, forcing an orderly winding-down process. A Failed Vision and a New Reality The dream of a new era for professional golf died quickly once the funding stopped. Phil Mickelson proclaimed LIV would be a game changer that brought the PGA Tour to its knees, but that never happened. It was never destined to become the “force for change and good,” that Bryson DeChambeau once mocked so laughably. According to Lee News Central , LIV amounted to nothing beyond a cash grab. Because it was always amoral at its core and utterly devoid of principles, failure was inevitable like so many other things. While he had previously collaborated with the brand on headcovers, this new deal expands their relationship to feature his own dedicated clothing collection. DeChambeau shared seven photographs announcing the news on social media alongside an enthusiastic message for his followers. “I’m excited for this one,” he wrote. “Headcovers were just the start… now I’m expanding my partnership with @swaggolfco into apparel!” The new collection drops November 19 online and in stores at Dick’s Sporting Goods and Golf Galaxy. item.title: NFL trade deadline deal tracker includes Jessie Bates, Kirk Cousins, and more
item.description: (Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL trade deadline is right around the corner. Teams have until 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, November 10, to make deals in an effort to either improve rosters for a playoff push, or prepare for a rebuild over the upcoming offseason. But some teams have not waited to push deals across the line. Monday began with the news that the Atlanta Falcons were sending defensive back Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars, as general manager James Gladstone tries to improve a defense that is already considered one of the best in the league. While we expect more deals to come, here is a running list of the trades that have gone down so far. This will be updated as new deals come through. Colts trade Josh Downs to Chiefs And we have another Colts trade. Indianapolis is trading wide receiver Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs, giving Patrick Mahomes another target in the passing game. Here are the full terms of the deal: Chiefs receive: WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick Colts receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick Chargers trade Daiyan Henley to Broncos The Broncos are adding on defense, acquiring linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Los Angeles Chargers in the rare trade between division rivals. Here are the full terms of the deal: Broncos receive: LB Daiyan Henley Chargers receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick Raiders trade Kirk Cousins to Vikings And there it is. After a poor showing on “Monday Night Football,” the Minnesota Vikings are trading for Kirk Cousins. The move brings Cousins back to Minnesota, reuniting him with Kevin O’Connell. It also paves the way for the start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas. Here are the full terms of the deal: Vikings receive: Kirk Cousins Raiders receive: A 2027 third-round pick. Titans trade Amani Hooker to Bills A defense that could use some help is getting it. The Tennessee Titans, having already traded Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, are sending safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills. Here are the full terms of the trade: Bills receive: S Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick Titans receive: A 2027 second-round pick Colts trade Keenan Allen to 49ers The trades are back on the docket in Indianapolis. After reportedly hitting the pause button over the weekend, the Colts are back in the headlines. Indianapolis is sending veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers, a team that has been hampered by injuries at that position. Here are the full terms of the trade: 49ers receive: WR Keenan Allen Colts receive: A 2027 sixth-round pick Eagles trade Arnold Ebiketie to Bengals Update: Or not! Apparently this deal has fallen through . The Eagles are not done making moves. On Tuesday, Philadelphia traded pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals, giving the AFC North contenders another presence on the edge. Here are the full terms of the trade: Bengals receive: EDG
item.content:encoded: (Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL trade deadline is right around the corner. Teams have until 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, November 10, to make deals in an effort to either improve rosters for a playoff push, or prepare for a rebuild over the upcoming offseason. But some teams have not waited to push deals across the line.
