Titans trade Amani Hooker to Bills A defense that could use some help is getting it. The Tennessee Titans, having already traded Jeffery Simmons to the Bears, are sending safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills. Here are the full terms of the trade: Bills receive: S Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick Titans receive: A 2027 second-round pick Colts trade Keenan Allen to 49ers The trades are back on the docket in Indianapolis. After reportedly hitting the pause button over the weekend, the Colts are back in the headlines. Indianapolis is sending veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers, a team that has been hampered by injuries at that position. Here are the full terms of the trade: 49ers receive: WR Keenan Allen Colts receive: A 2027 sixth-round pick Eagles trade Arnold Ebiketie to Bengals Update: Or not! Apparently this deal has fallen through . The Eagles are not done making moves. On Tuesday, Philadelphia traded pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Cincinnati Bengals, giving the AFC North contenders another presence on the edge. Here are the full terms of the trade: Bengals receive: EDGE Arnold Ebiketie Eagles receive: A 2027 sixth-round pick Eagles trade Jordan Davis to Jaguars The Jacksonville Jaguars are absolutely all-in on the 2026 season. After acquiring both Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux earlier in the day, James Gladstone added yet another piece, trading for defensive tackle Jordan Davis in a deal with the Philadelphia Eagles. Davis has tallied 31 tackles and 1.5 sacks this season, including a sack of J.J. McCarthy on Sunday in Philadelphia’s 19-11 loss to the New York Giants. The trade gives Anthony Campanile yet another talented player on the interior, and now Eagles general manager Howie Roseman has a pair of picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. Here are the full terms of the trade: Jaguars receive: DT Jordan Davis Eagles receive: A 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick Jets trade Andre Cisco to Lions The Detroit Lions are getting some help on defense. The New York Jets are trading safety Andre Cisco to Detroit. The safety is on an expiring contract, and the Jets — who at the moment have more than $80 million in available cap space for next year — are getting what they can now. Here are the full terms of the trade: Lions receive: S Andre Cisco Jets receive: A 2028 sixth-round selection Saints trade Davon Godchaux to Jaguars The Jacksonville Jaguars are not done adding to their defense. Hours after trading for safety Jessie Bates III, the Jaguars swung a deal with the New Orleans Saints to acquire defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. While Bates can patrol the deep third of the defense and gives defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile a flexible safety that can play both in the deep middle and down near that line of scrimmage, Godchaux gives Jacksonville another option along the defensive line. That is something the Jaguars needed to add after the team lost DaVon Hamilton for the season due to a torn quad. Here are the full terms of the trade: Jaguars receive: DT Davon Godchaux Saints receive: 2028 sixth-round pick ( which could elevate to a 2027 sixth-round pick if Jacksonville acquires one via trade or the compensatory selection formula) Falcons trade Jessie Bates III to Jaguars Trade deadline week kicked off in style with the Atlanta Falcons sending veteran safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars. For the Jaguars, it is a move to shore up the secondary as Jacksonville tries to maximize the current window of contention. For Atlanta, it is a move to get something for Bates ahead of his free agency, and with the Falcons currently looking at over $100 million in cap space, they might not receive a compensatory selection for Bates should he walk in free agency and Atlanta make the most of those resources. Here are the full terms of the trade: Jaguars receive: S Jessie Bates III Falcons receive: A 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick Cardinals trade Jacoby Brissett to Ravens With Arizona benching quarterback Jacoby Brissett, and the Ravens suddenly looking at life without Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley for at least the next few weeks as both are dealing with injuries, this move makes a good bit of sense. Brissett gets a chance to play on a team that is trying to stay in the playoff chase, the Ravens get a quarterback that gives them a chance to do just that, and Arizona … well maybe they could have handled things differently but they got some picks in return. Here are the full terms of the trade: Ravens receive: QB Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick Cardinals receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to Bears Now this was a big one. With the Chicago Bears trying to keep pace in the tough NFC North, and the defense remaining an issue, general manager Ryan Poles swung for the fences, bringing in defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons in a trade with the Tennessee Titans. Simmons paid immediate dividends, as he was stellar in his Chicago debut against the Seattle Seahawks. Here are the full terms of the trade: Bears receive: DL Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick Titans receive: A 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick, and a 2027 fourth-round pick Colts trade DeForest Buckner to 49ers Changes are coming in Indianapolis. After parting ways with general manager Chris Ballard, the Colts began moving players with an eye to the future. One of those deals saw Indianapolis send DeForest Buckner back to the San Francisco 49ers, returning the defensive lineman to the team that drafted him with the seventh-overall pick in the 2016 NFL Draft. Here are the full terms of the trade: 49ers receive: DL DeForest Buckner Colts receive: A 2027 fourth-round pick Colts trade Quenton Nelson to Seahawks Indianapolis started their impending fire sale with a move involving guard Quenton Nelson. Still one of the premier interior offensive linemen in the NFL, the Colts sent him to Seattle as the Seahawks look to shore up their offensive line. Here

item.title: Ole Miss lands Mississippi’s No. 1 WR recruit in 2029
item.description: Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Ole Miss lands Mississippi’s No. 1 WR recruit in 2029 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It was not a good week on the field for Ole Miss Football . Ole Miss lost to Georgia in embarrassing fashion, falling 42-7 . The loss dropped Ole Miss to 6-3 on the season, as they tumbled to 19th in the AP Poll. While Ole Miss took the loss on the field, they got a win on the college football recruiting trail on Tuesday, per Hayes Fawcett of Rivals. “Class of 2029 WR Matthew Fletcher has Committed to Ole Miss, he tells me for Rivals. The 6’3 200 WR is the No. 1 WR in Mississippi in the 2029 Rivals300. ‘This is where I see my future #HottyToddy'” Fawcett posted on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Fletcher is the top player for the class of 2029 out of Mississippi. He is currently ranked as a three-star recruit. Fletcher also spoke about why he chose Ole Miss, per Zach Berry of On3. “I love the school. They have been top of my list after I first visited for a practice,” Fletcher said. “Ole Miss is home to be honest.” Fletcher, who is currently a high school sophomore, chose the Rebels over offers from Florida, Florida State, LSU, and Mississippi State. “Ole Miss just felt like home to me from the beginning. The coaching staff has been great throughout this whole process and has made me feel like a priority,” Fletcher said. “I love the environment the coaches are building and the direction the program is headed. I feel like Ole Miss is the best place for me to develop not only as a football player, but as a person. After talking with my family and thinking everything through, I felt like this was where I wanted my future to be. Still looking at other schools, too, but this is where I see myself right now.” Fletcher is the second member of the class of 2029 to sign with the Rebels, joining Athlete Jordan Husband. Related: Michigan’s Kyle Whittingham in full YOLO mode with Tommy Carr, Bryce Underwood decision for Oregon game Related: Auburn lands 4-star OL recruit who previously committed to Miami

item.title: NFL reporter says emoji sums up Eagles' reaction to Bengals trade nix
item.description: ESPN/NFL Network reporter Mike Garafolo tweeted that the Philadelphia Eagles were not happy that a trade with the Cincinnati Bengals involving defensive end Arnold Ebiketie appears to have fallen through because of an issue with compensatory picks. "Vibes in the Eagles' building right now after this one fell through: 🤬," Garafolo tweeted . ESPN NFL analyst Field Yates credited Over the Cap contributor Nick Korte, considered an expert on compensatory picks rules, with helping the Bengals for the second time in three years, with tweets earlier that followed Ian Rapoport's announcement of the reported trade, which Rapoport later reported wasn't finalized . Sports agent Drew Rosenhaus appeared on ESPN's "Pat McAfee Show" and suggested that the trade may have fizzled because Ebiketie didn't want to play for the Bengals. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: NFL reporter says emoji sums up Eagles' reaction to Bengals trade nix

item.title: NFL trade deadline 2026: Denver Broncos latest news and rumors
item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at the scoreboard during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th at 2 p.m. MT, and our Denver Broncos could be an active team prior to the deadline. They have been widely connected to Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor in the days leading up to the deadline , but according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the team could explore adding a weapon or two to their offense. He mentions running back, tight end, and wide receiver as the positions that they could add. With Harvey injury and Badie also on IR and injuries across the offense, would expect Broncos to explore adding a weapon or two before trade deadline (RB, TE, WR). https://t.co/TSad3tJ2d3 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 31, 2026 Looking at the Broncos’ needs heading into the deadline, the most glaring one is running back. Now, the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman helps, but the Broncos still need more from the position. RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie are on the injured reserve, and veteran JK Dobbins has been struggling all season. So, adding another back to pair with Coleman would make sense. The question is, will they go big and add a Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall? Or make a smaller move for someone like Tony Pollard or someone else? Klis mentions wide receiver, and while it may not be the most pressing need right now, it could be in a few months. Jaylen Waddle has not performed as expected thus far; Courtland Sutton will be 32 next season and has a large cap hit(Also restructured his deal and could be off the team next season); Pat Bryant has been very good, but has been on the IR; Marvin Mims is a pending free agent, while Troy Franklin is buried on the depth chart. Could the Broncos be looking to add a wide receiver who could contribute to this team this season and moving forward? This doesn’t seem as likely, but I wouldn’t rule it out if the right deal comes their way. As for tight end, I don’t know. The only name that could move the needle and that might be available is Dallas Goedert, but is that even worth it? He would certainly improve that room, but the Broncos really do not utilize their tight ends in the passing game. Evan Engram has had a disappointing year, and blocking specialist Nate Adkins leads the group (and, funny enough, the team) in TD receptions with 3, but he only has 6 total catches thus far. We’ll be tracking all the Broncos news and rumors throughout the weekend and right up to the deadline. It’s supposed to be an active deadline, so we’ll see if our Denver Broncos make any splashes or not in the coming days. Some notable trade Candidates Colts RB Jonathan Taylor Colts WR Josh Downs Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. Titans RB Tony Pollard Eagles TE Dallas Goedert Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack Cardin

item.title: LaNorris Sellers Injury Update: Beamer Confirms Heisman Hope Is Alive
item.description: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images The temptation to rest South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers is growing loud among fans. Many worry his injured ankle could get worse if he plays on Saturday night. Coach Shane Beamer told reporters on Sunday that the team fully expects their star player to take the field. He disclosed the details of the injury and stated his position. Sellers limped to a game-winning touchdown against Texas A&M. Now he faces Arkansas, and the staff have already made a decision. Coach Beamer Confirms Sellers Status Beamer spoke directly about the tests Sellers took on Sunday. The results came back clean, which gives the staff confidence. “We fully expect him to play,” Beamer said, according to a report . He added that the player got some tests done and everything looked good with the results. The quarterback did not practice Sunday evening, and the team does not practice on Mondays. The schedule does not indicate Sellers is out. Beamer expects his Heisman Trophy candidate to be under center against the Razorbacks. “We feel good about his availability this weekend,” Beamer said. The coach noted that the only real issue is pain tolerance. “Right now, it’s nothing that concerns us aside from his pain tolerance and getting some of the swelling down in that ankle,” he explained. Why Sitting Him Is a Bad Move Sellers has already proven his worth with two huge moments this season. He pushed aside two Tennessee defenders for a score and then limped for a 41-yard touchdown against Texas A&M. These are signature moments that Heisman voters remember. The risk of sitting him now outweighs the benefit of rest. Arkansas has struggled terribly throughout almost the entire season, securing only a single SEC victory. It is the total number of wins against Power 4 teams. The Gamecocks cannot afford to lose to a bad team. Provided Sellers is healthy and cleared, he ought to play at Razorbacks Stadium this Saturday night. The talk of a College Football Playoff spot ends with a loss to the Razorbacks. A win keeps the dream alive for a trip to New York for the Heisman Trophy. When to Finally Bench the Star There is a time to rest a player, but this game is not it. The sole prudent option involves benching Sellers should the Gamecocks build a large lead in the second half. That would protect him from further injury without costing the team the win. Fans have been worried since the injury happened in the second quarter against the Aggies. Some think a high ankle sprain makes resting him a good idea. Beamer does not think it is a high ankle sprain, which changes the math. Healing from high ankle sprains often proves difficult and requires several weeks for full recovery. Sellers looks mobile enough on the field, even if the staff calls plays to protect him. A loss to Arkansas this weekend would render the Georgia matchup in two weeks meaningless nationally for the Gamecocks. Victories in the final three contests will send the Gamecocks to the College Footbal

The results came back clean, which gives the staff confidence. “We fully expect him to play,” Beamer said, according to a report . He added that the player got some tests done and everything looked good with the results. The quarterback did not practice Sunday evening, and the team does not practice on Mondays. The schedule does not indicate Sellers is out. Beamer expects his Heisman Trophy candidate to be under center against the Razorbacks. “We feel good about his availability this weekend,” Beamer said. The coach noted that the only real issue is pain tolerance. “Right now, it’s nothing that concerns us aside from his pain tolerance and getting some of the swelling down in that ankle,” he explained. Why Sitting Him Is a Bad Move Sellers has already proven his worth with two huge moments this season. He pushed aside two Tennessee defenders for a score and then limped for a 41-yard touchdown against Texas A&M. These are signature moments that Heisman voters remember. The risk of sitting him now outweighs the benefit of rest. Arkansas has struggled terribly throughout almost the entire season, securing only a single SEC victory. It is the total number of wins against Power 4 teams. The Gamecocks cannot afford to lose to a bad team. Provided Sellers is healthy and cleared, he ought to play at Razorbacks Stadium this Saturday night. The talk of a College Football Playoff spot ends with a loss to the Razorbacks. A win keeps the dream alive for a trip to New York for the Heisman Trophy. When to Finally Bench the Star There is a time to rest a player, but this game is not it. The sole prudent option involves benching Sellers should the Gamecocks build a large lead in the second half. That would protect him from further injury without costing the team the win. Fans have been worried since the injury happened in the second quarter against the Aggies. Some think a high ankle sprain makes resting him a good idea. Beamer does not think it is a high ankle sprain, which changes the math. Healing from high ankle sprains often proves difficult and requires several weeks for full recovery. Sellers looks mobile enough on the field, even if the staff calls plays to protect him. A loss to Arkansas this weekend would render the Georgia matchup in two weeks meaningless nationally for the Gamecocks. Victories in the final three contests will send the Gamecocks to the College Football Playoffs.

item.title: Seahawks’ Derick Hall’s Message to Klint Kubiak Before Raiders Game
item.description: Arizona Cardinals v Seattle Seahawks Getty Derick Hall is one of the key reasons the Seattle Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions. The 25-year-old is one of the top young stars on a stingy defensive unit that ranks fourth in the NFL in points allowed per game. That’s just a year removed after leading the Seahawks to the best defensive ranking in the NFL, allowing just 17.2 points per game. Hall posted two sacks in the Seahawks’ Super Bowl LX victory over the New England Patriots and parlayed that into a three-year, $42 million contract extension in the offseason. Things haven’t been perfect this season for Seattle as it’s been an up-and-down year. They’re 5-4 and in the thick of the NFC playoff race, but they’ve been forced to deal with key injuries to starters Sam Darnold and Zach Charbonnet. Seattle has been able to weather the storm and they’ve been able to pick up key victories, including handing the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss while also beating the Patriots in the season opener. Derick Hall’s Message For Former Seahawks Coordinator Klint Kubiak Entering Week 10, they’ll face off against a familiar face in the Klint Kubiak-led Las Vegas Raiders . Kubiak is obviously best known for his tenure as the offensive coordinator of the Seahawks, helping lead them to the Super Bowl last season before landing the Raiders head coaching job. “Klint’s just about ball,” said Hall in a one-on-one interview with Heavy Sports. “He’s a really really good guy, family man, big on his faith. Loves God, loves his family, and loves football. When you have all those three things, and you’re doing it the right way and working for you, success is going to come. But Klint, man, he just does all the things the right way. He’s a great offensive mind, one of the best in the game. Has all the motions, has all the movements, has all the things that can get you out of place. It’s about getting the call, getting lined up, trying to execute that to the best of our ability. Because we know Klint always got some stuff up his sleeve, as we saw last year when he was here with us, man. So great offensive mind. It’ll be am honor to play against him, and we’re looking forward to it.” When asked if he has a certain message for his former coach, Hall keeps it modest and said he’ll show his appreciation for the 39-year-old head coach before the game. “Probably just love him, love him up, but nothing else to say,” said Hall. “Just go to work.” Derick Hall Partners With Huggies For World Prematurity Day Hall is obviously one of the stars of the Seahawks, but his background story is beyond special. The 25-year-old is one of the top young stars on a stingy defensive unit that ranks fourth in the NFL in points allowed per game. Derick Hall’s Message For Former Seahawks Coordinator Klint Kubiak Entering Week 10, they’ll face off against a familiar face in the Klint Kubiak-led Las Vegas Raiders . Kubiak is obviously best known for his tenure as the offensive coordinator of the Seahawks, helping lead them to the Super Bowl last season before landing the Raiders head coaching job. “Klint’s just about ball,” said Hall in a one-on-one interview with Heavy Sports. “He’s a really really good guy, family man, big on his faith. Loves God, loves his family, and loves football. When you have all those three things, and you’re doing it the right way and working for you, success is going to come. But Klint, man, he just does all the things the right way. He’s a great offensive mind, one of the best in the game. Has all the motions, has all the movements, has all the things that can get you out of place. It’s about getting the call, getting lined up, trying to execute that to the best of our ability. Because we know Klint always got some stuff up his sleeve, as we saw last year when he was here with us, man. So great offensive mind. It’ll be am honor to play against him, and we’re looking forward to it.” When asked if he has a certain message for his former coach, Hall keeps it modest and said he’ll show his appreciation for the 39-year-old head coach before the game. “Probably just love him, love him up, but nothing else to say,” said Hall. “Just go to work.” Derick Hall Partners With Huggies For World Prematurity Day Hall is obviously one of the stars of the Seahawks, but his background story is beyond special. The 25-year-old was born premature by four months (at 23 weeks) and was given just a 1% chance of living. Doctors told his mother that even if Hall survived, he wouldn’t be able to live a normal life. His mother fought for him and Hall ended up not only living a normal life, he emerged as a top football star with the Seahawks drafting him in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The biggest message from Hall’s story is one of resilience and battling through when all odds are stacked against you. It’s the reason why he’s partnering with Huggies leading into World Prematurity Day (Nov. 15). “That’s 100% correct,” said Hall of the biggest message from his life story is being of resilience. “And more than anything, it takes a village to raise a child. The main piece for me is my mom. My mom was my advocate. Being a premie baby, you need someone to fight for. You need someone to advocate for you, so that being your mother, your father, your family, and then you have the secondary level of that, which is Huggies, and myself and my foundation. It’s just so huge to have that belief, that resilience, that fight, and know that someone is fighting for you. O “Obviously as a kid, a little infant baby, you can’t realize those things, but as you begin to grow, because these hardships can last for good bit of time in the adolescent years of their lif, you begin to see who’s been there for you and who’s the people who’s been doing the background work. Your parents advocating for yo, so that’s true to us about resilience, fight, toughness, grit, connection and then just having people to fight for you, getting your parents Huggies, and then having an opportunity to do this. Which is so special to me about giving back and having this opportunity myself.” Hall details his partnership with Huggies even further and the message he’s trying to spread through his foundation. “This partnership with Huggies came about obviously partially due to my story and NICU Awareness Month,” said Hall. “That’s really where it all started for me. This partnership, a lot of people know my story. I was a premie, given a 1% chance to live, and Huggies has been doing the the background work for premies for years and years. When I had this opportunity to partner with them, it was a no brainer for me and my foundation, the Derick Foundation, and my family. It’s just so key to have somebody fighting for you, being at bat, being combative for you and your family. It’s such a hardship because being a premie parent isn’t easy. “Going through all these hardships, knowing that there’s someone to show you the love, support, and connection in Huggies, and then the foundation of myself is just so huge,” said Hall. “You have World Premature Day coming up on November 15. So just in that opportunity, spread that light, spread that joy, let families know what Huggies is doing for premie babies in those moments, and let them know that there are people there to support you and help you through those hardships and those hard moments. It’s amazing. it’s something truly special, and I’m just looking forward to continue to grow this partnership and continue to know Huggies at a deeper level, and them obviously know me at a deeper level, so it’s amazing.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Seahawks’ Derick Hall’s Message to Klint Kubiak Before Raiders Game appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Kwanza Jones’ admission on owning Padres will catch fans’ attention
item.description: William Liang-Imagn Images Kwanza Jones’ admission on owning Padres will catch fans’ attention appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the San Diego Padres surrounded by rumors with the offseason in full swing, there could be fans who always have concerns when new ownership takes over, as Kwanza Jones and Jose Feliciano officially acquired the franchise in August. As the Padres look to free agency to boost the team for 2027 , Jones would speak about owning the team and the motivation she has to make the team great. While the annual general managers’ meeting is happening for MLB, Jones was asked by Sportico about the reason for investing in the San Diego baseball team and the reason behind it, despite the money aspect. Jones would emphasize the “heart” she has in making the team reach new heights. “Well, I’ll say, imagine a moment in a time where fans don’t have to doubt, don’t have to question, don’t have to wonder: Are the owners of the teams that they love, that they support, really involved, invested not just the money, but the heart? Because for me, that’s one of the most important things,” Jones said. “It’s the heart. So when we look at the Padres acquisition, how do we continue to build these bridges and unify?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kwanza Jones & Jose Feliciano, owners of the San Diego @Padres explain why it’s more than just money and the reason behind being ‘invested’ owners in their community and more. ⚾️ Does sport need more owners who care like them? pic.twitter.com/jl9NGqjHhv — Sportico (@Sportico) November 10, 2026 Kwanza Jones speaks more on owning the Padres Jones continues about acquiring the Padres along with her husband in Feliciano, and expressed how a big part of the job is to “win in the community” as well in San Diego. “What we want to do is win in the community too,” Jones said. “We want to win in bringing folks together; we want to win in creating opportunities. So it shouldn’t be mutually exclusive. It shouldn’t be a ‘Okay, owners just care about the bottom line.’ The bottom line is winning; the bottom line for some is ‘Okay, how much money can I make off of this?’ But that, for me, is not the bottom line only.” The Padres are looking to further improve after finishing with a 91-71 record, putting them second in the NL West, as they were eliminated in the playoffs by the World Series champions, the Milwaukee Brewers in four games. Related: Padres rumors: Insider confirms San Diego’s Tarik Skubal free agency interest Related: Bob Nightengale just asking questions about possible Fernando Tatis Jr., Mason Miller trades

item.title: Justin Jefferson should be happiest man alive after Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings finally have an answer for Justin Jefferson, and it is a familiar face who could help bring the best out of their superstar receiver again. Minnesota has reunited with Kirk Cousins , acquiring the veteran quarterback from the Las Vegas Raiders before the NFL trade deadline. For Jefferson, it is an opportunity to reconnect with a veteran player who already knows how to get him the football and helped him produce some of the best numbers of his career. Jefferson has not been quite the same dominant force this season, with Minnesota’s quarterback situation contributing to an offense that has struggled to find consistency. While he remains one of the most talented players at his position, his production has taken a noticeable dip compared with what Vikings fans have come to expect. But having a quarterback like Cousins who understands his routes, timing and tendencies could make a significant difference during the second half of the season. MORE: Brian Flores’ future with Vikings in serious danger after MNF loss to Bills Justin Jefferson’s production has taken a significant dip Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18). Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The numbers show why Cousins’ return is beyond welcoming for Jefferson. According to SumerSports figures, Jefferson averaged 108.2 receiving yards and 0.5 touchdowns per game when playing with Cousins. Without him, those averages dropped to 75.6 receiving yards and 0.39 touchdowns per game. That is a difference of more than 32 receiving yards per game. Justin Jefferson, rejoice 📈 https://t.co/zcnbDqaFWf pic.twitter.com/7kcODMN8FM — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 10, 2026 Jefferson’s 2026 numbers tell a similar story. Through eight games, Jefferson has recorded 31 receptions for 393 yards and four touchdowns. He is averaging 49.1 receiving yards per game, well below the standard he established during his best seasons. Jefferson finished 2025 with 1,048 yards and two touchdowns, while his 2024 campaign produced 1,533 yards and 10 scores. In 2022, with Cousins throwing him the football, Jefferson exploded for 1,809 yards and eight touchdowns, leading the league in receiving yards. MORE: Ex-NFL star says Kevin O’Connell’s future with Vikings in jeopardy after latest loss Vikings explored different options before trading for Kirk Cousins Minnesota’s quarterback search reportedly extended beyond Cousins. Jordan Schultz reported that the Vikings also inquired about Justin Herbert, Daniel Jones and Geno Smith before completing the trade. item.title: To thwart reverse engineering by agents, dev proposes blinding them
item.description: Now that LLMs can help analyze commercial software binaries and recreate their functionality, one software developer and student has created a project designed to make this process more difficult. Timo Zhang's project is called Blind LLM Agents (BLA), and as its name suggests, it attempts to interfere with efforts by AI agents to scrutinize app code. "Coding agents can reverse-engineer shipped packages, CLIs, and WASM in minutes," Zhang told The Register in an email. "Classic obfuscation was built for humans and static tools, not LLMs that reason about meaning. Blind LLM Agents is a protection layer for that threat model." Such agents can also help developers build alternatives to existing commercial software. Last month, Artcraft , a two-person development shop, released seven open-source apps that aim to be replacements for Adobe's commercial apps Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. Artcraft claims these apps are "clean-room reimplementations" written from scratch in Rust using Anthropic Opus 5.5. Setting aside the question of whether enlisting an AI model to reimplement an app really immunizes the creator from legal risk, those making apps face the possibility that someone will have an LLM probe published app binaries and reconstruct them through reverse engineering. There's in fact a framework for this, Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). Zhang has faced some criticism on social media for creating a limited barrier to copying other people's work (which at this point might simply be the work of another LLM). But not everyone accepts that all publicly accessible binaries should be easily available for review and reuse. BLA cannot prevent committed reverse engineering efforts, but it may add a bit of friction to the process when LLMs are involved. "It doesn't write app code — it hardens what you've already built," Zhang said. "A transform pipeline (plus MCP tools / an agent Skill) applies renaming, lane splitting, seed-derived string encryption, build polymorphism, WASM export renaming, decoys, self-seal integrity checks, and a coverage matrix that won't claim protection it can't prove. Behavior stays equivalent; recovery cost goes up." Zhang said various evaluations like red teaming and CrackMe challenges to recover keys or flags from hardened artifacts show that BLA is effective. "We also drive REA (a reverse-engineering agent) against those builds," he said. "Fail-to-break is the pass. CI tracks defense score, self-verifies integrity coverage, and checks functional equivalence. We raise the cost — we don't claim it is unbreakable." The project website says as much, noting that it raises the effort for analysis and adds decoy code, but doesn't promise protection against traditional interactive reverse engineering tools like Ghidra or Frida. Zhang said he's aware of other software projects that aim to interfere with AI, such as Poison Fountain for poisoning training data and Anubis for deterri
item.dc:creator: Thomas Claburn
item.content:encoded: Now that LLMs can help analyze commercial software binaries and recreate their functionality, one software developer and student has created a project designed to make this process more difficult. Timo Zhang's project is called Blind LLM Agents (BLA), and as its name suggests, it attempts to interfere with efforts by AI agents to scrutinize app code. "Coding agents can reverse-engineer shipped packages, CLIs, and WASM in minutes," Zhang told The Register in an email. "Classic obfuscation was built for humans and static tools, not LLMs that reason about meaning. Blind LLM Agents is a protection layer for that threat model." Such agents can also help developers build alternatives to existing commercial software. Last month, Artcraft , a two-person development shop, released seven open-source apps that aim to be replacements for Adobe's commercial apps Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. Artcraft claims these apps are "clean-room reimplementations" written from scratch in Rust using Anthropic Opus 5.5. Setting aside the question of whether enlisting an AI model to reimplement an app really immunizes the creator from legal risk, those making apps face the possibility that someone will have an LLM probe published app binaries and reconstruct them through reverse engineering. There's in fact a framework for this, Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). Zhang has faced some criticism on social media for creating a limited barrier to copying other people's work (which at this point might simply be the work of another LLM). But not everyone accepts that all publicly accessible binaries should be easily available for review and reuse. BLA cannot prevent committed reverse engineering efforts, but it may add a bit of friction to the process when LLMs are involved. "It doesn't write app code — it hardens what you've already built," Zhang said. "A transform pipeline (plus MCP tools / an agent Skill) applies renaming, lane splitting, seed-derived string encryption, build polymorphism, WASM export renaming, decoys, self-seal integrity checks, and a coverage matrix that won't claim protection it can't prove. Behavior stays equivalent; recovery cost goes up." Zhang said various evaluations like red teaming and CrackMe challenges to recover keys or flags from hardened artifacts show that BLA is effective. "We also drive REA (a reverse-engineering agent) against those builds," he said. "Fail-to-break is the pass. CI tracks defense score, self-verifies integrity coverage, and checks functional equivalence. We raise the cost — we don't claim it is unbreakable." The project website says as much, noting that it raises the effort for analysis and adds decoy code, but doesn't promise protection against traditional interactive reverse engineering tools like Ghidra or Frida. Zhang said he's aware of other software projects that aim to interfere with AI, such as Poison Fountain for poisoning training data and Anubis for deterring bots and scraping. BLA, he said, is different. It's for hardening shipping code against reverse engineering and LLM-aided analysis. ®

item.title: McTominay reveals heart treatment two days before Scotland’s World Cup opener
item.description: Midfielder was in hospital before Haiti match ‘I had to get the shock on my heart,’ says McTominay Scott McTominay has revealed he was in hospital under sedation to have a “shock on my heart” just 48 hours before Scotland began their World Cup campaign against Haiti in June. McTominay’s absence from training at the time was put down to a stomach complaint. It emerged in August that the Napoli midfielder would undergo surgery to remedy an irregular heartbeat. The operation took place the next month, causing McTominay to miss Scotland’s opening to the Nations League. The player has now disclosed that the matter arose in the United States as Scotland prepared for their World Cup bow. Continue reading...

item.title: Sanwo-Olu appoints Akinyemi as acting MD LAWMA
item.description: .Reviews management structure By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu has finally appointed Olajuwon Akinyemi as the acting Managing Director of the Lagos State Waste Management Authority, LAWMA. By the appointment, Akinyemi succeeded former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin who was forced to resign following intractable waste management challenges across the state. When contacted, the state Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, on Tuesday evening, confirmed the appointment. According to Wahab, the new MD, who was the former Executive Director of Operations, will also serve in the capacity of Executive Director, Finance. Also, in the coming days, new officers would be redeployed in the restructuring effort of the management staff. This comes following reports of forced resignation of former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin over the seemingly intractable waste management challenges across the state. This laid to rest earlier reported appointment of , Dr. Hassan Sanuth, Director Sanitation Services – Office of Environment in the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources as acting MD. However, Sanuth was temporarily drafted to LAWMA to assist in waste management pending appointment of substantive managing director. On October 19, indications emerged that Governor Sanwo-Olu has directed Gbadegesin to resign amid persistent refuse accumulation across the state. It was gathered that the governor became increasingly dissatisfied with Gbadegesin’s handling of the waste management crisis and had asked him to step down. Earlier in September 2026, during an inspection of the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota, Sanwo-Olu handed a strong warning against further failure to stop the menace announcing plans to overhaul the agency for effective management, describing Gbadegesin’s inability as “sabotage” According to an inside source, “the governor’s displeasure stemmed from the slow pace of waste evacuation and the alleged failure of Gbadegesin to act promptly on directives aimed at addressing the crisis. “The governor was at the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota a month ago and was dissatisfied with the state of things. He gave instructions that immediate action be taken on the matter, as he has declared a state of emergency on waste management. “The governor was upset when he observed that the situation had not improved despite his clear directive. So, over the weekend, he asked him to resign, although he is begging and has reached out to some prominent Lagosians to beg on his behalf.” Also, residents across Lagos have repeatedly complained about worsening waste collection, with refuse accumulating along road medians, streets and major highways. The situation has raised concerns about envir

item.title: Embrace HIV testing as routine healthcare-Lagos govt urges residents
item.description: . Extends free screening to staff, trade fair visitors By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has urged residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. Meanwhile, the state government has extended free HIV testing and counselling services to public servants and visitors to the ongoing 2026 International Trade Fair as part of efforts to promote early diagnosis and expand access to HIV prevention and treatment. The interventions, implemented by the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency (LSACA), are aimed at bringing HIV-related services closer to residents, encouraging routine testing and ensuring that individuals who require further care are linked to appropriate treatment facilities. At the Public Service Week health screening exercise, the Head of Service, Lagos State, Mr Bode Agoro, officially opened the free screening programme and urged public servants to prioritise their health by taking advantage of the opportunity. Agoro said access to preventive healthcare, including HIV screening, was essential to building a healthy, productive and efficient workforce. He encouraged workers to embrace regular health checks and utilise the confidential testing, professional counselling and information on HIV prevention, transmission and treatment provided through the exercise. In a related intervention, LSACA commenced free HIV testing and counselling services at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), as part of activities at the 2026 International Trade Fair. The exercise, which began on Friday, November 6, is scheduled to run for 10 days, ending on Sunday, November 15. It provides visitors, exhibitors, traders and other participants with access to confidential HIV screening, counselling, preventive health information and guidance on accessing treatment and care where necessary. The Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr Folakemi Animashaun, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to ensuring that HIV prevention, testing and treatment services remain accessible, confidential and free from discrimination. Animashaun said knowing one’s HIV status was an important step towards preventing new infections and improving health outcomes, noting that early diagnosis enables individuals who test positive to commence treatment promptly and maintain healthy, productive lives. She urged public servants, Trade Fair participants and residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. The LSACA chief executive also emphasised the importance of collaboration with Ministries, Departments and Agencies, development partners, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in expanding access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care services. Animashaun therefore, urged members of the public to visit the LSACA screening centre at the Lagos Pavil

item.title: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 live updates: Super Heavy rocket moved to launch pad for 1st Starship double landing test
item.description:
Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. To see his latest project, you can follow Tariq on Twitter @tariqjmalik.

SpaceX is counting down to make history with the launch of its Starship Flight 15 mission on Friday, Nov. 13 , with liftoff scheduled for 5:45 p.m. EDT (2245 GMT) at Starbase, Texas. Starship Flight 15 will attempt to land both Starship Ship and Super Heavy Booster. It will be the first-ever full recovery of an orbital rocket and spacecraft, if successful. Follow our Starship Flight 15 coverage here as SpaceX completes its final prelaunch work for the launch, which will also deliver 26 new Starlink V3 satellites into orbit. Flight 15 livestream | SpaceX | Starship | Starship V3 explained November 10, 2026 – 2:42 PM SpaceX sets Nov. 13 launch date for Starship Flight 15 Artist's illustration of SpaceX catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket, something the company expects to do on the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) Hello, Space Fans, and welcome to our coverage of SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight , the first ever to attempt twin landings of the Starship Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage. SpaceX has officially set the launch date for Flight 15 for Friday, Nov. 13, at 5:45 p.m. EDT (2145 GMT) . That puts launch just about 3 days away and Space.com will provide live coverage of the potentially historic flight, the first full recovery of an orbital rocket. Space.com Spaceflight Writer Josh Dinner will be reporting live from near SpaceX's Starbase , Texas site for the launch, with myself (Tariq Malik), Spaceflight and Tech Editor Mike Wall and other team members tracking the flight remotely for you here. SpaceX has already test-fired the engines on its Starship Flight 15 vehicles. Today, SpaceX moved Super Heavy Booster 22 , the first stage for Flight 15, to the launch pad for vehicle stacking. Here are some photos of that move: Super Heavy moved to the launch pad at Starbase. Booster 22 is the first Super Heavy V3 booster planned to return to the launch site for catch and was used for final catch testing upon arrival, including a suspended squeeze test at catch height https://t.co/iYTX1e6DEH November 10, 2026 We'll be updating this page regularly in the days ahead counting down to SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launch (and landings). So check back for updates each day.

item.title: ‎States must contribute to pension protection fund to benefit from minimum pension — PenCom DG
item.description: ‎–It is big shame for some state retirees to be paid ₦5,000’ ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA — The Director-General of Nigeria’s National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms. Omolola Bridget Oloworaran, said on Tuesday that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can become eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎She stated this at the official launch of the Minimum Pension Guarantee Scheme and the unveiling of PenCare, a pension industry-funded healthcare initiative designed to provide low-income retirees with access to essential medical services free of charge. ‎‎The event was held at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. ‎She said about 170,000 retirees are expected to receive the minimum pension of ₦52,500, including those who were previously receiving less than that amount. ‎‎“Every eligible retiree who earns below ₦52,500 will be uplifted to ₦52,500. So, of course, as I said, there is no discrimination if you are within the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). ‎‎“However, there is an eligibility criterion at the same level. We are making it a requirement that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can be eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎“So, we will work out that modality at the state level because we all know that the fund needs to be sustainable. If people are not contributing, we will run out of funds, and we cannot start a laudable initiative like this and then, years from now, somebody says it has stopped working because people are not contributing. ‎‎“So, we are working on modalities for the states to start contributing. But, as of now, it does not apply only to federal workers. Even private-sector workers are receiving these minimum pensions. ‎‎“As I said in my speech, 54 per cent of the total number of retirees who fall below the minimum pension work in the private sector, even though the private sector is not the majority employer. Essentially, 65 per cent or more of private-sector retirees are earning less than ₦52,500. ‎‎“So, when we tell them to contribute to the Pension Protection Fund, there is a reason for that. They form a large chunk of the money we need.” ‎‎On whether anything was being done to ensure that retirees from states also benefit from the minimum pension, as some of them still receive about ₦5,000 monthly, the PenCom DG said it was shameful to pay someone such an amount, although she doubted whether any state actually paid such a paltry sum. ‎‎“Frankly, that is a big shame. What we have done is that we have started working with the states to ensure that they pay retirement benefits to their retirees and also put a plan in place to review pensionable inflation. ‎‎“I mean, receiving ₦5,000 is unacceptable. I do hope it is not true. I will ask my team to confirm. ‎‎“But ultimately, what we are trying to do is get all the states into the scheme. Once you get into the scheme and start contributing to the Pension Protection Fund, the fund can protect the retiree
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: ‎–It is big shame for some state retirees to be paid ₦5,000’ ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA — The Director-General of Nigeria’s National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms. Omolola Bridget Oloworaran, said on Tuesday that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can become eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎She stated this at the official launch of the Minimum Pension Guarantee Scheme and the unveiling of PenCare, a pension industry-funded healthcare initiative designed to provide low-income retirees with access to essential medical services free of charge. ‎‎The event was held at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. ‎She said about 170,000 retirees are expected to receive the minimum pension of ₦52,500, including those who were previously receiving less than that amount. ‎‎“Every eligible retiree who earns below ₦52,500 will be uplifted to ₦52,500. So, of course, as I said, there is no discrimination if you are within the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). ‎‎“However, there is an eligibility criterion at the same level. We are making it a requirement that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can be eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎“So, we will work out that modality at the state level because we all know that the fund needs to be sustainable. If people are not contributing, we will run out of funds, and we cannot start a laudable initiative like this and then, years from now, somebody says it has stopped working because people are not contributing. ‎‎“So, we are working on modalities for the states to start contributing. But, as of now, it does not apply only to federal workers. Even private-sector workers are receiving these minimum pensions. ‎‎“As I said in my speech, 54 per cent of the total number of retirees who fall below the minimum pension work in the private sector, even though the private sector is not the majority employer. Essentially, 65 per cent or more of private-sector retirees are earning less than ₦52,500. ‎‎“So, when we tell them to contribute to the Pension Protection Fund, there is a reason for that. They form a large chunk of the money we need.” ‎‎On whether anything was being done to ensure that retirees from states also benefit from the minimum pension, as some of them still receive about ₦5,000 monthly, the PenCom DG said it was shameful to pay someone such an amount, although she doubted whether any state actually paid such a paltry sum. ‎‎“Frankly, that is a big shame. What we have done is that we have started working with the states to ensure that they pay retirement benefits to their retirees and also put a plan in place to review pensionable inflation. ‎‎“I mean, receiving ₦5,000 is unacceptable. I do hope it is not true. I will ask my team to confirm. ‎‎“But ultimately, what we are trying to do is get all the states into the scheme. Once you get into the scheme and start contributing to the Pension Protection Fund, the fund can protect the retirees of those who participate.” ‎‎She expressed joy that many Nigerians, especially retirees, had started receiving the minimum pension. ‎She also said that the Commission had given healthcare cards to some people to test the system before the official launch. ‎‎“Because, before you pilot something, you want to test it with a group of people to make sure that it is working as intended. So, it has been rolled out, and Nigerians can now go into a hospital and enjoy free healthcare. ‎‎“So, as I said, what we did today was symbolic. But from today, anybody who does not have their card can go to their PFA and request one.” ‎‎Answering a question on why the Commission decided to launch the service when elections were forthcoming, and whether it was not a plot to influence voters, the DG said she did not involve herself in politics. ‎‎She rhetorically asked: “Is there ever a bad time to do good for ordinary Nigerians, to put a smile on people’s faces? And you know, I do not get involved in politics. I never talk about politicians or anything political. We just do our work.” ‎‎She said PenCom was only a regulator. ‎“We do not get involved in politics at all. You can ask my people. But my response to that will be: every day you wake up, we try to see what we can do to improve the lives of ordinary Nigerians. When we did the pension boost last year, there was no election. ‎‎“She also said that the Commission had paid a ₦32,000 consequential increase last year when there was no election. ‎‎“It is not something that is geared towards the election. It just happens to be coming at this point. In fact, this was supposed to be done in September when we were expecting the President himself to attend, but the industry said we needed to do some other things, and we shifted Pension Week to October. ‎‎“You will notice that we had said this was going to be done in October, but we could not do it then. So, we shifted it from September to October because of the industry. Later, we decided to settle for today. ‎‎“So, everything we are doing, we are just doing our work. We do not see elections. I do not. Frankly, anybody else might see it, but I am responsible for PenCom. I do not see elections. I do not see competition. I am just doing my work. ‎‎“But guess what? If my work makes the President look good, then it means I am doing what he hired me to do. And on that question, I will also say this: I have been going for press conferences, and people ask me, ‘You are doing all of this. How are you going to make sure it is sustainable?’ Even then, when I am supposed to talk politics, I still do not talk politics. You understand? So, we do not do politics here. ‎‎“But, to be fair, it is a President who has appointed the right person to lead, who has appointed the right board and leadership in PenCom, and we are executing his vision for the industry. That is how I see it. And lastly, I would just say: does it matter what time it is, provided ordinary Nigerians are benefiting?” The post ‎States must contribute to pension protection fund to benefit from minimum pension — PenCom DG appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
item.description: Google has announced a " super network " upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it's adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one. Google's MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google's Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel. With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google's blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn't mention either network, saying only that it supports "two of America’s best 5G cellular networks." Read full article Comments

item.title: Awujale stool: Adele-in-Council sues Abiodun, challenges reconstituted interregnum committee
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council has dragged the Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, and members of the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council before the state High Court, Ijebu-Ode, challenging what it described as an unlawful attempt to displace the traditional administrative structure of Ijebuland. Other defendants sued alongside Gov Abiodun are the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs as well as members of the recently reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council including High Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu Ode, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa, Prof Jide Ajayi, the Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen Bakare, the Babalaje as well as Chief Alade Shote, the Otun Balogun The suit dated November 5, 2026 and marked HCJ/201/2026 according to a statement from the Media office of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council and supporting court documents made available to journalists on Tuesday seeks to establish the authority of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council to oversee the traditional and administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum following the transition of the late Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Kayode Adetona. The nine members of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council led by the Adele and Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland, Olorogun Dr Sonny Kuku, are asking the court to declare that the Adele system is the only legitimate traditional administrative authority recognised by the native law, customs and ancestral practices of the Ijebu people during the period between the reigns of successive Awujales. They are also challenging the establishment and subsequent reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, describing the arrangement as alien to Ijebu customary law and inconsistent with the Ogun State Chiefs Law. In the substantive suit, the plaintiffs are seeking a declaration that neither the state governor nor the relevant government authorities possess the power to create or reconstitute an administrative council capable of displacing the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during an interregnum. They are further asking the court to set aside the purported reconstitution of the AIAC and the appointments of the fifth to eighth defendants, describing the appointments as irregular, illegal, unconstitutional, null and void. The plaintiffs also want a perpetual injunction restraining the governor, the relevant ministries and other government officials from interfering with or bypassing the customary administrative functions of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council. Similarly, they are seeking an order restraining the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council from holding meetings, parading themselves or exercising traditional, civil or financial administrative authority over Ijebu-Ode under the disputed AIAC arrangement. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council has dragged the Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, and members of the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council before the state High Court, Ijebu-Ode, challenging what it described as an unlawful attempt to displace the traditional administrative structure of Ijebuland. Other defendants sued alongside Gov Abiodun are the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs as well as members of the recently reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council including High Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu Ode, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa, Prof Jide Ajayi, the Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen Bakare, the Babalaje as well as Chief Alade Shote, the Otun Balogun The suit dated November 5, 2026 and marked HCJ/201/2026 according to a statement from the Media office of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council and supporting court documents made available to journalists on Tuesday seeks to establish the authority of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council to oversee the traditional and administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum following the transition of the late Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Kayode Adetona. The nine members of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council led by the Adele and Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland, Olorogun Dr Sonny Kuku, are asking the court to declare that the Adele system is the only legitimate traditional administrative authority recognised by the native law, customs and ancestral practices of the Ijebu people during the period between the reigns of successive Awujales. They are also challenging the establishment and subsequent reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, describing the arrangement as alien to Ijebu customary law and inconsistent with the Ogun State Chiefs Law. In the substantive suit, the plaintiffs are seeking a declaration that neither the state governor nor the relevant government authorities possess the power to create or reconstitute an administrative council capable of displacing the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during an interregnum. They are further asking the court to set aside the purported reconstitution of the AIAC and the appointments of the fifth to eighth defendants, describing the appointments as irregular, illegal, unconstitutional, null and void. The plaintiffs also want a perpetual injunction restraining the governor, the relevant ministries and other government officials from interfering with or bypassing the customary administrative functions of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council. Similarly, they are seeking an order restraining the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council from holding meetings, parading themselves or exercising traditional, civil or financial administrative authority over Ijebu-Ode under the disputed AIAC arrangement. The statement partly reads the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council is hereby seeking “A declaration that under the native law, custom, tradition, and ancestral usages of the Ijebu-Ode people, the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council is the sole, valid, and historically recognized traditional administrative authority entitled to manage the interim traditional and local administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during an interregnum following the transition of the Awujale of Ijebuland. “A declaration that the unilateral creation, establishment, or reconstitution of an administrative body known as the “Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council” (AIAC) by the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Defendants is alien, unknown, and offensive to the native law, customs, traditions, and ancestral usages of the Ijebu-Ode people, and completely inconsistent with the provisions of the Chiefs Law of Ogun State. “A declaration that neither the Chiefs Law of Ogun State nor any applicable customary law empowers the 1st to 3rd Defendants to arbitrarily invent, sustain, or reconstitute an “Interregnum Administrative Council” to sideline, supplant, or replace the ancestral Adele system and traditional council structures during an interregnum” The plaintiffs are also asking for “an order setting aside the purported reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC) and the handpicked appointments of the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th Defendants by the 1st to 3rd Defendants as highly irregular, illegal, unconstitutional, null, void, and of no effect whatsoever. “An order of permanent injunction restraining the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Defendants, whether by themselves, their agents, officials, ministries, or privies, from interfering with, bypassing, or disrupting the customary administrative functions of the Plaintiffs as the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during the period of the interregnum. “An order of permanent injunction restraining the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th Defendants from holding meetings, parading themselves, or attempting to exercise any traditional, civil, or financial administration over the town and stool of Ijebu-Ode under the guise or authority of the illegal, purported newly reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC)” It would be recalled that traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode and members of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, constituted by the state government in August last year following the death of the Awujale and paramount ruler of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Adetona, recently resolved to dissolve the council and transition into the Adele Oba Awujale in Council to oversee the affairs of the ancient town pending the emergence of a substantive Awujale. The decision was reportedly reached at a meeting involving the Ilamuren, Pampa, Odi and other chiefs of Ijebu-Ode, where the traditional leaders unanimously adopted a resolution mandating members of the AIAC to step down from their existing positions and assume membership of the newly constituted Adele Oba Awujale in Council. According to the resolution signed by the Chairman of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, Olo’rgun Dr Sonny Kuku, the chiefs said the decision to transition from the interregnum administration to the Adele Oba Awujale in Council was informed by their consideration of the existing traditional and statutory frameworks governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution. The government had however announced the reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), reaffirming its legal authority to oversee the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale Addressing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale group, the government declared that “the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy legislation in Ogun State”. It stated further that “neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Obas and Chiefs Law of Ogun State 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the management of the Awujale stool”. The government thereafter announced the reconstitution of the council with the following members; Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode – Chairman, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa as Secretary, while Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen O. Bakare, Babalaje and Chief Alade Shote, Otun Balogun are to serve as members. The government said the reconstituted council would continue to discharge the legally recognised administrative and traditional responsibilities of the AIAC until a new Awujale was appointed and crowned. The Fusengbuwa ruling house had earlier dragged Abiodun, the Awujale kingmakers and five others before the High Court sitting in Ijebu-Ode, seeking orders compelling the completion of the process for the selection of the next Awujale and Paramount Ruler of Ijebuland. item.title: Only Rainbow Coalition can guarantee Tinubu’s victory in Bayelsa – PDP
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The Peoples Democratic Party ,PDP, in Bayelsa State has claimed that the Rainbow Coalition is central to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects in the state, pledging to mobilise 300,000 votes for the President in the 2027 general elections. The state PDP chairman and leader of the coalition, Chief George Alabh Turnah, made the declaration in a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Media and Communication, Kevin Loveday-Egbo. Turnah said the coalition would take its campaign for Tinubu’s re-election to communities across the state, with a grassroots mobilisation strategy targeting undecided voters ahead of the 2027 elections. He described the National Rainbow Coalition as a platform for engaging voters, explaining that the group would use its community-level outreach to highlight what it considers the achievements of the Tinubu administration and canvass support for his second term. The PDP chairman said the coalition was committed to expanding its mobilisation network across the state, adding that its target was to secure 300,000 votes for the President. He also challenged the All Progressives Congress, APC, to mobilise an additional 500,000 votes, bringing the combined target of both parties to 800,000 votes. “The Rainbow Coalition has pledged 300,000 votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Bayelsa State. We are tasking the APC to deliver 500,000 votes to bring the total number of votes for the APC to 800,000 out of the one million, one hundred and fifty thousand Permanent Voter Cards collected in the state,” Turnah said. He said the coalition would intensify its grassroots engagements across Bayelsa as preparations gather momentum for the 2027 general elections. The post Only Rainbow Coalition can guarantee Tinubu’s victory in Bayelsa – PDP appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
item.description: An artist’s concept depicting a Voyager spacecraft. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight this historic milestone with two events. On Tuesday, Nov. 17, NASA invites the world to participate in “Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day” by creating a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset. NASA has created a website that enables smart phones and tablets to flash “VGR”, Voyager’s call sign, in morse code. For more information about how to participate in “Shine Bright for Voyager Light-Day,” visit: go.nasa.gov/shinebright Everyone is encouraged to capture photos or videos of their light-day signal and share it on social platforms, tagging @NASA. On Thursday, Nov. 19 at 12 p.m. EST (9 a.m. PST), NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California will host a moderated discussion with mission members and NASA leadership about the status of Voyager 1 and 2, the unique science the twin probes continue to gather in interstellar space, and the challenges of keeping the spacecraft operating for so long over such vast distances. A Q&A with media and other audience members will follow. In addition, there also will be a preview of the upcoming NASA+ Voyager documentary, planned for release in 2027 for the mission’s 50th anniversary. The event will take place in NASA JPL’s von Kármán Auditorium, where JPL hosted Voyager briefings during the spacecraft’s grand tour of the outer planets. The participants will be: Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, Washington Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Southern California, and professor of planetary science, Caltech Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager, NASA JPL Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager, NASA JPL Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist, Princeton University Learn where to watch online at: https://www.nasa.gov/live U.S. media interested in attending the event in person must RSVP by Monday, Nov. 16 to Josh Smooha at: josh.smooha@jpl.nasa.gov . To be considered for onsite credentials, foreign national media must RSVP no later than Thursday, Nov. 12. Media interested in participating virtually must RSVP no later than two hours before the event. NASA’s media accreditation policy is available online. For almost half a century, the agency’s Voyager mission has blazed a trail through space. Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 were designed to explore the outer planets by taking advantage of a planetary alignment that occurs once every 176 years. Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012. Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight this historic milestone with two events. On Thursday, Nov. 19 at 12 p.m. EST (9 a.m. PST), NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California will host a moderated discussion with mission members and NASA leadership about the status of Voyager 1 and 2, the unique science the twin probes continue to gather in interstellar space, and the challenges of keeping the spacecraft operating for so long over such vast distances. The participants will be: Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, Washington Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Southern California, and professor of planetary science, Caltech Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager, NASA JPL Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager, NASA JPL Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist, Princeton University Learn where to watch online at: https://www.nasa.gov/live U.S. media interested in attending the event in person must RSVP by Monday, Nov. 16 to Josh Smooha at: josh.smooha@jpl.nasa.gov . Media interested in participating virtually must RSVP no later than two hours before the event. NASA’s media accreditation policy is available online. For almost half a century, the agency’s Voyager mission has blazed a trail through space. Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 were designed to explore the outer planets by taking advantage of a planetary alignment that occurs once every 176 years. Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012. Following a different trajectory, Voyager 2 entered in 2018. Both spacecraft continue to provide unique scientific observations of the environment beyond the heliosphere, the protective bubble created by the Sun. Managed by Caltech in Pasadena, California, NASA JPL built and operates the Voyager spacecraft. NASA’s Deep Space Network , also managed by NASA JPL, enables communication with the distant probes. The Voyager mission is funded by NASA’s Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. item.title: Nobody Said The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Was This Funny
item.description: Though I’ve never played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time until now, I’ve heard people sing its praises for years. Mostly, this revolved around its impossibly high score of 99 on Metacritic, its influential open world and combat design, and its memorable dungeons. But none of those ardent fans bothered to tell me that this classic game has some genuinely hilarious moments. Because the game was originally released 28 years ago, a spoiler-free experience is pretty much off the table for me. But the goofs and gags? Those are all 100% fresh.

item.title: Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – No fewer than three persons have reportedly been killed following an attack by gunmen on a mining site in Jol community, Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 6pm on Tuesday, when the assailants reportedly stormed the mining site and opened fire on people in the area. A resident of the community, Bulus Shen, who confirmed the incident, told newsmen that the gunmen arrived at the mining site in the evening and began shooting sporadically. Shen said the attack threw the community into panic, adding that three persons were reportedly killed in the incident. The spokesperson of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the attack. Tengwong condemned the killing, describing the incident as disturbing and unacceptable. He called on security agencies to urgently investigate the attack, apprehend those responsible and strengthen security around rural communities to prevent further loss of lives. Efforts to get further details from security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .
